title: Es el jardín más venenoso del planeta y todas sus plantas son mortales
summary: Jane Percy, duquesa de Northumberland, se inspiró en los hermosos jardines de los Medici en Florencia, Italia y diseñó un espacio especializado al que llamó Poison Garden (Jardín del Veneno), dentro del complejo del castillo de Alnwick (Northumberland, Reino Unido). Todas las plantas de este jardín ...
content:
Jane Percy, duquesa de Northumberland, se inspiró en los hermosos jardines de los Medici en Florencia, Italia y diseñó un espacio especializado al que llamó Poison Garden (Jardín del Veneno), dentro del complejo del castillo de Alnwick (Northumberland, Reino Unido).
Todas las plantas de este jardín podrían matarte
Ese castillo fue escenario de varias películas, entre ellas Robin Hood: príncipe de los ladrones (1991), Harry Potter y la piedra filosofal (2001), Harry Potter y la cámara de los secretos (2002).
El objetivo de la duquesa era recolectar y exponer al público visitante todas las plantas que pudieran causar problemas al hombre por su toxicidad o veneno.
De este modo, acabó construyendo un jardín botánico de 14 hectáreas, especializado en unas 100 plantas cuyo atractivo es, paradójicamente, el veneno que contienen.
En el portón de la entrada, aparece un mensaje junto a una calavera, en el que puede leerse: "Estas plantas pueden matar".
Los carteles que secundan el recorrido del jardín no dejan lugar a dudas. Junto a la consabida calavera, el mensaje no puede ser más claro: "¡No tocar, oler ni comer ninguna planta!".
Otro mensaje, dirigido específicamente al público infantil, recuerda que "Los niños deben ir acompañados de adultos en todo momento".
Todas las especies que hay en este Jardín son venenosas y gran parte de ellas son mortales.
Veneno en todas las plantas y flores
Algunas de las plantas que se pueden contemplar aquí son: la adormidera, el beleño, la belladona, la coca, la cicuta, el lirio de los valles, la mandrágora, la nuez vómica, el perejil gigante, el ricino, la trompeta de ángel.
Es el único jardín del mundo en donde los jardineros cuidan las plantas con traje de protección y máscara y solo se admiten visitas con un guía especializado.
Pese a las estrictas reglas del lugar hubo casos de desmayos, debido a los efluvios venenosos que algunas de estas flores lanzan al aire.
Por su condición de plantas venenosas, su cultivo también está vigilado. Los arbustos están muy aislados unos de otros, y los jardineros tienen cuidado de que las semillas no salgan fuera del jardín, para impedir que se reproduzcan en el exterior.
El Jardín del veneno de Jane Percy tiene un enorme éxito desde su inauguración en 2005, y en la actualidad es una de las atracciones turísticas más visitadas del Reino Unido.
Otra característica poco conocida es que muchas de estas plantas las tenemos en nuestros jardines, y no lo sabemos. 
Desde luego, uno de los motivos de este éxito es el morbo, que Jane satisface y justifica desde su mismísima página web: "Me preguntaba por qué tantos jardines en todo el mundo se centran en el poder medicinal de las plantas y no en su capacidad de matar, Me pareció que la mayoría de los niños que conocía estarían más interesados en escuchar cómo una planta mata, cuánto tiempo tardarías en morir si la comieras y cómo de grotesca y dolorosa sería la muerte".

title: TikTok employees said they knew about child safety issues, but execs failed to act
summary: TikTok was repeatedly warned by its own staffers about risks its platform posed to child safety, according to court records obtained by NPR. The publication reports that employees were frustrated over TikTok executives failing to appropriately act on concerns they raised, including minors bypassing ...
content:
TikTok was repeatedly warned by its own staffers about risks its platform posed to child safety, according to court records obtained by NPR. The publication reports that employees were frustrated over TikTok executives failing to appropriately act on concerns they raised, including minors bypassing age-restricted content, and appearing in “transactional sexual content” the company could financially benefit from.
TikTok employees said they knew about child safety issues, but execs failed to act
‘I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn’t think the harms are severe enough.’
The previously unreported depositions of TikTok staffers were filed in federal court in March, and connected to a multi-district litigation initiated in 2022 that brings together hundreds of lawsuits alleging that TikTok, Meta, Snap, and Google knew that they social media platforms are harmful to children, and failed to disclose those risks.
One deposition from Reagen Maher, who held senior safety and investigations positions between 2021 and 2024, described flagging the prevalence of “transactional sexual content” to then-TikTok CEO V Pappas, regarding minors stripping on TikTok’s Live feature in exchange for “gifts” that can be converted into real currency. Forbes reported on the issue in 2022, and Maher said the company was already aware of the sexual exploitation concerns before the article was published.
“I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn’t think the harms are severe enough,” Maher said in an excerpt from an internal chat with a colleague. “Put simply, senior leaders know about this issue. There are some ongoing projects to fix parts of it, and frankly, I’m hoping [that] this article puts a fire behind other potential solutions.”
Another deposition from TikTok’s former head of safety Eric Han says he was concerned about harmful algorithm “rabbit holes” in 2020, describing them as having a “real contagion effect” regarding “suicidal ideation and behavior” in an internal TikTok report. Despite flagging that “minor safety is an urgent issue that we must address effectively,” Han said that TikTok failed to warn parents of the potential dangers of their child using the platform.

title: Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with MS
summary: Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis: "Not happy at all" Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis, more than five years after announcing she had been told she had the chronic condition. Applegate, 54, shared the news ...
content:
Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis: "Not happy at all"
Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis, more than five years after announcing she had been told she had the chronic condition.
Applegate, 54, shared the news in a double episode of her podcast MeSsy, where she and co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler discuss life with multiple sclerosis. Applegate had taken a break from the podcast in recent weeks. She said Tuesday she had taken that time to process the new information.
Applegate said that "all of a sudden, a few years ago," her doctor wanted to take her off an infusion treatment and see how her B cells reacted. The cell count didn't increase or decrease after the treatment stopped, which began "kind of a study into my diagnosis," Applegate said. Eventually, her doctor had surprising news: Applegate had never had multiple sclerosis at all.
"She came into my room and said, 'Congratulations, you don't have MS,' " Applegate said. "I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy."
Multiple sclerosis, or MS, is a disease where the body's immune system attacks the central nervous system. Symptoms vary from person to person, according to the National Multiple Sclerosis Society, and there are multiple types of the disease. The condition has no known cause, and its progression is impossible to predict.
Dr. Marwa Kaisey, an associate professor at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center department of neurology, said on the podcast that almost one in five people who have been told they have multiple sclerosis "didn't actually have it." Misdiagnoses with the condition are "fairly common," she said, because there is no one test for it.
Applegate said at the time of her initial diagnosis, she underwent tests including a spinal tap and MRIs. Scans showed lesions on her brain, she said.
Applegate said that she continues to have debilitating symptoms that affect her daily life and mobility.
"You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I'm better," Applegate said. "If anything, I've gotten worse. So I'm back at square one where I don't know what's going on with me. And that's going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?"
The investigation will begin next week, she said.
Applegate has previously described living with symptoms including numbness, an off-balance feeling, and a tingling sensation in the limbs. She said in a 2022 interview with The New York Times that she "can't walk without a cane."
In the same interview, she said she used a wheelchair during filming of the Netflix hit "Dead To Me," and the show's script was adjusted to accommodate her symptoms. In 2023, Applegate said her symptoms might lead to her giving up acting on camera. She said Tuesday that she has physical therapy three times a week.
After she was officially diagnosed with the disease, she became an outspoken advocate for MS. On Tuesday, she said the misdiagnosis made her feel "like I let everybody down."
"It's very unnerving and it's really confusing for me," Applegate said.

title: Rubio aborda la crisis energética con los cancilleres de India y Emiratos Árabes en Bombay
summary: El secretario de Estado de EE. UU., Marco Rubio, se reunió este martes en Bombay con el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de la India, S. Jaishankar, y el canciller de Emiratos Árabes Unidos (EAU), Abdulá bin Zayed Al Nahyan, para discutir la situación energética entre socios comerciales. "Fue excelent...
content:
El secretario de Estado de EE. UU., Marco Rubio, se reunió este martes en Bombay con el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de la India, S. Jaishankar, y el canciller de Emiratos Árabes Unidos (EAU), Abdulá bin Zayed Al Nahyan, para discutir la situación energética entre socios comerciales.
"Fue excelente reunirme con el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de la India, Dr. S. Jaishankar, y con el ministro de Exteriores de EAU, Abdullah bin Zayed, para discutir la seguridad energética regional y avanzar en nuestras prioridades económicas compartidas", afirmó Rubio a través de un mensaje en la red social X.
El representante de Washington se encontró previamente con Jasihankar, tras lo que aseguró que el acuerdo comercial bilateral, que lleva en fase de negociación más de un año y medio, se encuentra en su fase final.
"Estamos muy, muy cerca. Yo diría que estamos tan cerca como se puede estar sin tener un acuerdo firmado. Creo que queda un pequeño número de puntos por resolver, así que creo que se concretará en breve", afirmó Rubio a la prensa tras su reunión.
Por su parte, el embajador de EE. UU. en la India, Sergio Gor, calificó las conversaciones de "productivas" y destacó los avances en materia de defensa, energía, tecnologías emergentes y comercio para mantener el impulso en la relación bilateral.
Este es el segundo viaje de Rubio a la India en lo que va de año, después de su visita en mayo a Nueva Delhi, durante la que se reunió con el primer ministro, Narendra Modi.
"En realidad creo que no venimos lo suficiente y creo que deberíamos venir más", agregó Rubio a los medios, y recordó que tanto la secretaria de Comercio como el director del FBI y el vicepresidente de EE. UU. han visitado el país recientemente.
Tras completar su agenda en Bombay, Rubio se trasladará a la localidad de Jamnagar, en el estado occidental de Guyarat, donde se encuentra la refinería de crudo más grande del mundo.
Allí se prevé que se reúna con el magnate indio Mukesh Ambani, propietario de la planta de Reliance Industries, que ha centrado la atención de la Casa Blanca por su capacidad para procesar el pesado crudo venezolano.

title: Quién es Xavier Becerra, el hijo de una familia mexicana que busca gobernar California frente a Trump
summary: Ana Milena Varón Xavier Becerra, que se encamina a hacer historia como el primer gobernador latino de California en más de 150 años, advierte en entrevista con EFE que Donald Trump "siempre encuentra la manera de causar daño" y promete hacerle frente desde la experiencia de haber crecido en una fami...
content:
Ana Milena Varón
Xavier Becerra, que se encamina a hacer historia como el primer gobernador latino de California en más de 150 años, advierte en entrevista con EFE que Donald Trump "siempre encuentra la manera de causar daño" y promete hacerle frente desde la experiencia de haber crecido en una familia inmigrante y mexicana de clase trabajadora.
Becerra, (Sacramento, California,68 años) se proyecta como el seguro ganador de la Gobernación de California, según la última encuesta de Activote que lo sitúa con un 62,8 % de apoyo entre los votantes probables, frente al 37,2 % de Steve Hilton, el candidato republicano y amigo del mandatario estadounidense.
"Este señor (Trump) siempre encuentra modos de hacer daño en cualquier lugar. Así que no dudo de que durante el tiempo que yo empiece la gobernatura va a estar tratando de hacer daño", aseguró en un encuentro en Los Ángeles.
Pero para el demócrata, la clave está en "saber cómo luchar" contra las políticas de Trump que afecten a las comunidades, una capacidad que en parte vincula con su trayectoria política: más de 24 años en la Cámara de Representantes, su paso como primer latino por la Fiscalía General de California (2017-2021) y su gestión como secretario de Salud y Servicios Humanos de EE.UU. (2021-2025).
El hijo de inmigrantes mexicanos y obreros
El próximo 3 de noviembre, Becerra podría nuevamente hacer historia al convertirse en el primer gobernador latino de California en más de 150 años. Al preguntarle si esto representa un desafío adicional, responde que el verdadero reto está en cambiar el rumbo del estado desde la experiencia de quienes, como sus padres, han tenido que luchar para salir adelante.
"Lo que cambia es la dirección del estado bajo alguien que es hijo de migrantes, hijo de familia obrera, hijo que tuvo que luchar para ser el primero en ir y conseguir un grado de una universidad", explica.
Esa historia familiar, añade, le ha dado una visión clara de las prioridades del Estado Dorado, como se le conoce a California: gobernar en beneficio de la clase trabajadora, un enfoque que, sostiene, también podría contribuir al bienestar del resto del país.
"Viendo mis padres trabajar bien duro, siempre teniendo los retos frente de ellos y que cumplieron, así que yo tengo que cumplir sabiendo que va a haber mucho reto: Donald Trump, los incendios, el costo de la energía", señala.
California es el estado más poblado de EE.UU. con 39,5 millones de habitantes, de los cuales el 41 % es latino. Desde 2025 han sido de los más afectados por las redadas migratorias de la administración Trump.
No es inmigrante
Pero esa historia familiar se ha convertido en motivo de controversia durante la campaña. Hilton, nacido en el Reino Unido, cuestionó el relato de Becerra como hijo de inmigrantes: su madre, María Teresa, es inmigrante mexicana originaria de Jalisco, pero su padre, Manuel, nació en Sacramento y creció en Tijuana, por lo que era ciudadano estadounidense de nacimiento.
"Perdí todo respeto para mi contrincante Steve Hilton, cuando atacó a mi papá porque la familia se tuvo que ir a México porque los americanos no querían darle trabajo a mi abuelo. Me da rabia porque no conoce al inmigrante. Steve Hilton, un inmigrante, no conoce al inmigrante de California y quiere ser gobernador", reprochó el demócrata.
La controversia sobre sus raíces familiares enlaza con otra de las prioridades que Becerra plantea para California: fortalecer los vínculos con México, no solo por su historia personal, sino también por la importancia económica y comercial de la relación bilateral.
Para el demócrata, California, la cuarta economía del mundo, tiene mucho que ganar de una cooperación más estrecha con su vecino del sur.
"Así que para mí no solo porque soy hijo de herencia mexicana, pero porque sé la importancia de México para California. Vamos a crecer eso, ese enlace y hacer más fuerte esa relación", indicó.
Encarar a Trump
Sus críticos han cuestionado que haya centrado parte de sus discursos de campaña en atacar a Trump. Sin embargo, Becerra defiende que son las medidas implementadas por la Casa Blanca las que están afectando al país y en especial a la clase trabajadora, por lo que asegura que no se quedará callado.
"Nada es fácil cuando uno tiene a Donald Trump en la presidencia haciendo todo más costoso lo que tenemos que hacer es luchar contra la locura que viene de Washington", puntualizó.
Agencia EFE.

title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems
summary: The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing services and products developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns tied to the Chinese AI startup’s operations in China, according to the Department of Homeland Se...
content:
The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing services and products developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns tied to the Chinese AI startup’s operations in China, according to the Department of Homeland Security. The order goes beyond banning DeepSeek’s own product, but also covers third-party products and services built using DeepSeek technology, though agencies can request exceptions.
The DHS raised concerns about DeepSeek’s handling of user data, warning that sensitive information from US government users could potentially be accessible to Chinese authorities under Chinese law, the order said.
The move comes amid intensifying tech competition in AI between the US and China. The Chinese AI model challenges its U.S. rivals, including OpenAI and Meta, with low-cost open-weight models.
China pushed back against the U.S.’s move. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Tuesday that Beijing opposes “overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues,” according to an official briefing. “We will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises,” the spokesperson added.
The U.S. has already taken steps to limit DeepSeek’s use in government. A law passed in December 2025 targeted its use in intelligence’s national security systems. The latest order extends the restrictions to federal civilian agencies, covering both new purchases and existing IT systems.
Meanwhile, China is reportedly considering export restrictions on 23 AI-related technologies, including chip designs and certain advanced AI models, to address security and misuse risks, Bloomberg reported last week.
The Chinese AI lab has faced scrutiny from governments and regulators across the globe since its R1 reasoning model shook the AI industry in January 2025, triggering a sharp sell-off in Nvidia shares.
The U.S. accused DeepSeek and five other Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba and Moonshot AI, of using large-scale model distillation to extract information from American AI systems, according to a September report.
In addition, OpenAI and Anthropic have separately raised concerns about DeepSeek’s alleged use of model distillation, a technique that uses outputs from one AI model to train another. Earlier this year, OpenAI told U.S. lawmakers it had observed suspected attempts by DeepSeek to distill its models, while Anthropic said it had identified unauthorized attempts by DeepSeek and other Chinese AI labs to collect outputs from Claude.

title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
summary: Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap. When the app detects a person, or a group of people, have their eyes closed in a photo it will automatically present ...
content:
Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap. When the app detects a person, or a group of people, have their eyes closed in a photo it will automatically present users with a new Open Eyes Quick Action that appears as an icon over the image providing easy access to the new feature.
Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
When the mobile app detects closed eyes in a photo it will present users with a new Open Eyes Quick Action tool.
Being able to easily save an otherwise great photo by opening a subject’s eyes has been a feature in Adobe’s Photoshop Elements for nearly a decade, but as DPReview points out, Elements sources the replacement from another photo of the subject with mixed results depending on variations between the two images. Open Eyes in Lightroom mobile instead relies on generative AI so the replacement eyes match the lighting and pose, and the app will use other images of the same person in your Lightroom library as reference so the open eyes will accurately match the color, size, and shape of their own.
You can perform a similar fix in other Adobe apps like Photoshop using its own generative AI tools, but it’s not a one-tap fix, and it’s not free. Those using the free version of the Lightroom mobile app can try the Open Eyes feature twice before they’re given a prompt to subscribe to an Adobe Creative Cloud plan that includes more credits for its various AI-powered tools, according to DPReview.

title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
summary: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain - Date: - October 20, 2026 - Source: - University of British Columbia - Summary: - Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can...
content:
Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- University of British Columbia
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage. Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow. This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue.
- Share:
Statins are among the most important medications for preventing cardiovascular disease. By lowering cholesterol, they have helped save millions of lives and reduce the likelihood of heart attacks and strokes. However, these benefits can come with unwanted effects. Some patients develop muscle pain or weakness, while a small number experience serious muscle breakdown that can potentially cause kidney failure.
Scientists at the University of British Columbia (UBC), working with colleagues at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, have identified a molecular mechanism that helps explain these complications. Their findings, published in Nature Communications, could guide the development of safer statins that maintain their cholesterol-lowering benefits while minimizing muscle damage.
How Statins Trigger a Harmful Calcium Leak
To investigate what happens inside muscle cells, the researchers used cryo-electron microscopy, an advanced imaging method that allows scientists to examine protein structures in remarkable detail. Their investigation centered on the ryanodine receptor (RyR1), a protein that regulates the movement of calcium within muscle cells.
Under normal conditions, this protein functions as a controlled gateway, releasing calcium when muscles need to contract. The researchers found that statins can interfere with this process by holding the channel open. As a result, calcium escapes continuously into areas where it should be carefully regulated, creating conditions that can injure muscle tissue.
"We were able to see, almost atom by atom, how statins latch onto this channel," said lead author Dr. Steven Molinarolo, a postdoctoral researcher in UBC's department of biochemistry and molecular biology. "That leak of calcium explains why some patients experience muscle pain or, in extreme cases, life-threatening complications."
Three Statin Molecules Reveal the Mechanism Behind Muscle Damage
The researchers concentrated on atorvastatin, a commonly prescribed medication for lowering cholesterol. Although this particular drug was the main focus, their results suggest that similar interactions could occur with other medications in the statin family.
One of the most striking discoveries was the unusual way statin molecules attach to the calcium channel. Rather than acting individually, three molecules occupy a specific pocket within the protein. The first binds while the channel is closed, making it more likely to open. Two additional molecules then enter the pocket and hold the channel open, allowing calcium to continue leaking.
"This is the first time we've had a clear picture of how statins activate this channel," said Dr. Filip Van Petegem, senior author and professor at UBC's Life Sciences Institute. "It's a big step forward because it gives us a roadmap for designing statins that don't interact with muscle tissue."
This detailed understanding could give drug developers a way to address the problem at its source. By modifying the specific features of statin molecules that interfere with muscle proteins, scientists may be able to reduce unwanted effects without compromising the drugs' ability to control cholesterol.
A Potential Path Toward Safer Cholesterol Drugs
More than 200 million people worldwide use statins. Although severe muscle injury occurs in only a small percentage of patients, less serious problems such as soreness, weakness, and fatigue are considerably more widespread. These symptoms can be disruptive enough that some people discontinue their medication, potentially losing important protection against cardiovascular disease.
The discovery could eventually help researchers create treatments that are easier to tolerate, allowing more patients to continue taking medications that reduce their risk of heart attacks and strokes.
Achieving this level of understanding required exceptionally detailed imaging. Working with the high-resolution macromolecular cryo-electron microscopy facility at UBC's faculty of medicine, the team was able to observe precisely how statin molecules interact with the muscle protein. These structural insights connect a longstanding drug safety concern to a specific molecular process, providing valuable information for future medication development.
"Statins have been a cornerstone of cardiovascular care for decades," Dr. Van Petegem said. "Our goal is to make them even safer, so patients can benefit without fear of serious side effects."
Although additional research and drug development will be needed before these findings translate into new treatments, they offer a promising direction. For millions of people who depend on statins to protect their hearts, future medications with fewer muscle-related complications could make treatment more comfortable and improve everyday quality of life.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of British Columbia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Steven Molinarolo, Carmen R. Valdivia, Héctor H. Valdivia, Filip Van Petegem. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals sequential binding and activation of Ryanodine Receptors by statin triplets. Nature Communications, 2025; 16 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-66522-0

content:
Robots still aren’t that good at picking things up, despite billions of dollars of investment and endless videos fed into deep learning models.
That may be about to change, thanks to a manipulation architecture built by Eka Robotics, which encompasses a force-sensitive gripper and a new kind of deep-learning model. Founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the startup just closed an $150 million Series A round that values it at $1.45 billion post-money, led by venture funds a16z and F-Prime.
“They are already exceeding superhuman performance for certain tasks, and so we think over the next few months there will be superhuman performance in many dexterous manipulation tasks,” Raghu Raguram, the a16z general partner who co-led the fundraising round, told TechCrunch.
In an era of never-ending robotic demonstrations, Eka’s capabilities are shocking veteran robot builders.
Kris Hauser, a professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, said it had a “wow factor” compared to other robot demos he saw recently. The Eka robot “was able to adapt to a large number of different objects without retraining,” Hauser said, adding that it also had an aspect of “humanness, creepy humanness that it would try over and over again if it failed the first time.”
Another roboticist, who asked for anonymity because of their work at a frontier lab, told TechCrunch that seeing Eka’s robot in action was an emotional experience, comparable to when robots first achieved reliable legged locomotion five to ten years ago. Take a look for yourself:
What’s notable here? How smoothly and rapidly the robot moves. It can pick up about 1,500 objects that weigh up to 1 kg in an hour, compared to about 600 for a human; Eka says it reliably picks up objects more than 95% of the time. And the robot arm is strong enough to hurt itself as it moves that quickly. That indicates, per the frontier lab observer, that “they have a lot of trust in their algorithm not breaking the robot. I wonder how many robots they broke along the way?”
When the frontier lab roboticist met Eka’s robot, they handed it a raspberry, the lab’s apparent favorite test item. “The experience of a big, heavy robot rushing towards my arm and then slowing down just in time and very gently touching me is a feeling that I am, as we speak, carrying this feeling in my body,” they told TechCrunch.
How not to squish the raspberry
These capabilities are a consequence of how the foundational model was built. Rather than a vision-language-action model — which is trained to understand the relationship between language, visual inputs, and actions — the schema here is a vision-force-action model, which focuses on the relationship between language, force inputs, and actions. Critics of the current direction of generative AI robotics models, like Rodney Brooks, say that they will fail without an attempt to represent force and touch; Eka’s results suggest such critics have a point.
“Vision is not the primary way in which you close this last millimeter problem,” Eka co-founder Agrawal told TechCrunch. “Vision tells you roughly where the object is, what the pose is, but the actual grabbing, the actual searching is happening through forces.”
Eka had to design a unique robotic hand that was more flexible than traditional grippers, and included more force sensors; it reacts to contact, which is why it doesn’t crush the raspberry. The founders are cagey about how they achieved that for obvious competitive reasons, but it comes down to using a physics simulator to model the multiple forces the robot will encounter as it attempts to grasp something, and using that to create a reinforcement learning environment that can be run at scale. They say they can generate thousands of hours of robot experience in minutes.
“Rather than being limited to the data that you’re collecting from, say, human demonstrations, Eka is pushing through reinforcement learning this approach where the robot can surpass any kind of demonstrations that are given to it,” Hauser said. “What’s really exciting is that they’re able to not be limited to the data that is presented to them for training.”
Agrawal and Haarnoja, who first met in graduate school at the University of California, Berkeley, are leading researchers in the field of reinforcement learning for robotics control. Eka’s key bet was that this technique could be done at scale through simulation, rather than relying on videos collected by gigworkers or robot operators performing tasks over many hours. Simulation was key to achieving their robot’s reliable manipulation, a feat that in the past that has proven more difficult for tasks that require interacting with objects, rather than avoiding them.
“What EKA is bridging is the generality-performance gap, which plagues a lot of modern robotics,” Agrawal argues.
Making a general-purpose robot useful
Right now, the most generalizable physical AI models—the ones that can attempt lots of different tasks—aren’t particularly good at them. But AI models trained to be highly capable at a single task may not close the business case for a company: The promise of generative AI is that robots can quickly learn multiple tasks, even novel ones.
The current approaches are good at producing robots that are more generally intelligent than before — Astra, ChatGPT’s latest LLM, can operate a robot in an unfamiliar setting and perform tasks with it, but slowly and at a high cost. The promise of a model like Eka’s is that it handles the physicality while a more general model makes decisions about how to solve a problem. Astra, for example, might know that plates get stacked in a cupboard when they come out of the dishwasher, but Eka’s model is capable of picking up a dish without breaking it.
“Most of the field has been focusing on the planning,” Eka co-founder Haarnoja says, “so they approach from the top: high-level intelligence, pushing that down towards the physical.

title: Inspired Capital closes $450M fourth fund as New York pushes back on Silicon Valley’s gravitational pull
summary: Inspired Capital, the early-stage firm founded in 2019 by Alexa von Tobel and Penny Pritzker, has closed its fourth fund with $450 million in commitments. The new capital will bring the firm’s assets under management to nearly $1.4 billion, von Tobel tells TechCrunch. The raise comes as venture doll...
content:
Inspired Capital, the early-stage firm founded in 2019 by Alexa von Tobel and Penny Pritzker, has closed its fourth fund with $450 million in commitments. The new capital will bring the firm’s assets under management to nearly $1.4 billion, von Tobel tells TechCrunch.
The raise comes as venture dollars are piling up on the West Coast. Between 2020 and the end of 2025, the Bay Area had raised $352 billion for VC funds — roughly 46% of all U.S. venture capital, according to PitchBook. Last year, that percentage shot up even higher, with Bay Area firms locking down 55% of the total new commitments to U.S. venture funds.
New York-based Inspired’s new fund is a reminder that capital is accruing elsewhere, too. In fact, Inspired is growing: it closed a $330 million third fund in early 2024, following a $281 million second fund and its $200 million debut fund.
Despite having money to invest, von Tobel says the firm is sticking to its formula. Inspired backs roughly 10 companies a year, which can be anywhere between “napkin” stage and Series A, writing checks between $1 million and $15 million. Pritzker, the former U.S. Commerce Secretary, remains an active co-founder in the firm.
With six years of investing experience under her belt, von Tobel is now willing to talk about results, too. She says that 12 companies across the firm’s first two funds have become unicorns, representing about 15% of the portfolio. “Ten of them have passed $100 million in revenue, four have crossed $400 million and one has crossed $500 million,” she says.
Perhaps more relevant to the firm’s limited partners, Inspired counts more than 10 exits, including MosaicML (acquired for $1.3 billion in June by Databricks), DeepTune (which Mercor acquired in July for an undisclosed amount), and Saturn (snapped up last year by Snap).
Another portfolio company, TeamShares, a fintech startup that buys up other businesses, went public in June through a special purpose acquisition vehicle. Von Tobel claimed the firm’s second fund ranks in the top 5% of its cohort by all metrics, though she declined to share cash-on-cash returns, citing the relative newness of the firm.
To be clear, Inspired is not squarely focused on New York. Its portfolio is split roughly 45% East Coast, 45% West Coast and 10% elsewhere. That balance reflects the way that startups grow, she says. “A company that’s getting quite big in Silicon Valley often wants and needs a second talent footprint, and New York becomes really important,” she says.
Of course, for others, New York is the only choice. On that front, von Tobel says she has been pitched by at least 10 founders in recent weeks who selected New York specifically to avoid hiring job-hopping employees who have little allegiance to any one company, as is often the case in San Francisco.
Von Tobel definitely doesn’t dismiss the Valley. She says that someone from her team is on the ground in the Bay Area every week, and that she’s in the area routinely, too. “We have to pay extreme attention to both [coasts],” she says.
As for strategy, she describes a firm that picks themes early and avoids the herd as much as possible. While many companies chase AI applications, for example, Inspired has backed physical AI and quantum computing startups, she says. Inspired came upon the creator-commerce platform ShopMy by following that thesis.
Where Inspired isn’t so different is in its penchant for backing serial entrepreneurs. Von Tobel says roughly a third of the firm’s portfolio is by repeat founders.
Asked about her stance on secondaries, she says Inspired will sell “a few chips” once companies reach multi-billion-dollar valuations, but it tends to keep more than 90% of its ownership, mostly using secondaries to add to positions in breakaway portfolio companies. That said, Inspired will lead later primary rounds if it misses an early one, and it has written checks for companies that are already valued above $100 million, according to von Tobel.
Von Tobel, who launched her online financial learning platform LearnVest on the TechCrunch 50 stage in 2009 and sold the company six years later to Northwestern Mutual for a reported $375 million, insists that Inspired’s strongest edge is patience and its ability to combine the best of both coasts.
“We bring West Coast ambition with East Coast financial discipline,” she says.

title: Wii Sports is back on the Switch 2, and it rules
summary: Wii Sports holds an important place in Nintendo’s history. It’s the best-selling piece of software the company has ever made, one that permeated culture in surprising ways, and its success helped rejuvenate Nintendo after a period of steady decline. It also kicked off one of the company’s most impor...
content:
Wii Sports holds an important place in Nintendo’s history. It’s the best-selling piece of software the company has ever made, one that permeated culture in surprising ways, and its success helped rejuvenate Nintendo after a period of steady decline. It also kicked off one of the company’s most important and unassuming franchises. While subsequent sports titles from Nintendo never sold quite as well as the original Wii Sports, they’ve become a fixture for each new console, much like a new Mario Kart or Pokémon. And now the Switch 2 has its own version, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, and it’s the best so far.
Wii Sports is back on the Switch 2, and it rules
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is quietly one of the console’s most important games.
You’d be forgiven for not realizing that Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is launching this week. The game is coming out during a particularly hectic time for new video game releases, and it’s sandwiched between two flashier Switch 2 titles in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave and the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Amid all of that, it’s easy to forget a game about thumb wrestling and bowling. But Sports Resort is also a refined and expansive version of the concept, and one that will likely become a constant over the Switch 2’s life.
The core of the game is the same as always: giving you a bunch of athletic activities — they’re not exactly all “sports” — that require some form of motion controls to play. That means swinging a Joy-Con controller to simulate using a tennis racket or tossing a bowling ball. There are 12 sports in all, and they vary quite a bit. The aforementioned returning favorites tennis and bowling are joined by things like skateboarding, thumb wrestling, and flying a plane.
What makes the game work is its simplicity. Almost each activity is incredibly easy to pick up; I don’t know much about golf, but it only took me a minute or so to get down the fundamentals of swinging a club using a Joy-Con. This means that Sports Resort excels as an arcade-style experience, the kind of game you pull out when friends are over and you want to have some fun. Thumb wrestling is ideal for this. It’s so simple — you move your hand back and forth and use a single button to try and “pin” your opponent — yet gets extremely intense and fun in the competitive two-player mode. And unlike IRL thumb wrestling, no one can actually cheat.
There are some exceptions to the general simplicity. I still find basketball to be a little too complex, and I just can’t seem to figure out a successful strategy in table tennis. But there are enough games in Sports Resort that you’re almost certain to find a handful of favorites you’ll stick with, so having a few duds isn’t the end of the world. There’s also a decent amount of depth, both in terms of the skill ceiling for games — I have spent hours trying to perfect the spin on my bowling release — but also the various modes for each sport. Bowling, for instance, includes the returning option to play with 100 pins at once, which is chaotic as it sounds.
But the biggest addition to Sports Resort is that it now takes place in an open world. That may sound strange for a collection of arcade games, but it also allows it to introduce three new activities that are centered on exploring the beautiful island setting. There’s prop plane (where you hold the Joy-Con like a paper airplane to fly), power cruising (where you hold two Joy-Con horizontally, like the handlebars of a Jet Ski), and skateboarding (where you use the Joy-Con’s mouse controls to simulate controlling a tiny skateboard). There are competitive ways to play these games, like a skateboard race, but I’ve spent most of my time with a sightseeing mode where the goal is to find as many landmarks and secrets across the resort as you can within a five-minute time limit. It’s sort of like a more fleshed-out version of the free roam mode in Mario Kart World. The island is surprisingly detailed and interesting to explore, with lots of caves and hidden paths, and the three modes of transportation let you check it out via land, water, and air.
These exploration-focused modes add a nice new dimension to the experience, fitting snugly within the more traditional sports while offering a very different vibe. I’ve become particularly drawn to skateboarding — there’s something very satisfying about pulling back on the Joy-Con to simulate pushing a board — especially since you can collect items that let you purchase new clothes and other accessories to customize your character.
One of the biggest keys to Nintendo’s success during the Switch era has been consistency. Even in the midst of a tumultuous period for the broader games industry, the company has managed to put out a steady stream of games, many of which have had a surprisingly long life. Nintendo’s biggest hits aren’t always what you expect. The first Nintendo Switch Sports has sold more than 18 million copies, topping beloved games like Super Mario Bros. Wonder and Splatoon 3.
A little over a year into its existence, that style of perennial seller is exactly what the Switch 2 needs, the kind of game that people pick up alongside Mario Kart when they buy a new console. Wii Sports showed just how transformative a game like that can be, and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is quietly keeping that spirit alive.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort launches on the Switch 2 on October 22nd.

title: Final Fantasy dips back into the SNES golden era with Resonance
summary: Final Fantasy is a lot different than it used to be. While many of the early Final Fantasy titles look and play similarly to each other, the series has since grown to encompass blockbuster games like Final Fantasy XVI and the gargantuan Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy, which don’t play much like th...
content:
Final Fantasy is a lot different than it used to be. While many of the early Final Fantasy titles look and play similarly to each other, the series has since grown to encompass blockbuster games like Final Fantasy XVI and the gargantuan Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy, which don’t play much like the classics. But there’s still an audience for retro RPGs and old-school Final Fantasy games, especially thanks to the HD-2D style that mixes gorgeous pixel art with detailed 3D graphics to great effect. Square Enix has made a bunch of HD-2D games already, like the remakes of early Dragon Quest titles, but this week, it’s launching the first HD-2D Final Fantasy game: Final Fantasy Resonance.
Final Fantasy dips back into the SNES golden era with Resonance
Square Enix’s latest HD-2D game carries the Final Fantasy name — and a lot of what makes the franchise great.
Resonance, thanks to the HD-2D art, kind of looks like what the classic Final Fantasy games feel like in my memory, but I was surprised at how old-school Resonance feels to actually play, too — which, for the most part, is a good thing. In Resonance, I’ve spent a lot of time wandering around a big world map to get from place to place, tackling random battles along the way and investigating little sparkles to pick up items. The towns have a familiar feel, with the classic inn, item shop, and weapons shop setup. Similarly, battles are traditional turn-based fights, so I’ve found myself spending a lot of time in various battle menus to plan out my attacks. Enemies even flash right before they attack, just like in older RPGs.
At times, Resonance can almost feel rudimentary; I’ve recently been working my way through Final Fantasy VII Remake again ahead of Revelation, and Remake’s action-heavy fights feel much more contemporary. But there’s something soothing about Resonance’s familiar patterns. I really like just grinding through some random baddies to level up.
The story is pretty standard fare, at least during the 10 hours I’ve played. You play as Rain, a plucky blonde hero who is morally pure and fights for those less fortunate than him. After a great magical crystal is destroyed, you and your best bud Lasswell head out on an adventure to stop the destruction of other crystals. So far, Resonance’s story hasn’t done a lot to innovate on a familiar formula — I’ve already come across two people who have amnesia, a JRPG staple — but it all moves along breezily enough that it’s not a huge deal.
Resonance isn’t all old-school, though, as there are a lot of modern touches. In fights, enemies have health bars and stagger bars, forcing you to be strategic instead of just mashing basic attacks; it’s usually smarter to whittle down a stagger bar by exploiting weaknesses through magic and skills. You can speed up fights and even skip long attack animations (of which there are many). On the world map, you can fast travel to any location you’ve already visited, which is especially useful during the multipart side quests. In dungeons, you can teleport from a save near a boss fight back to the entrance if you need to resupply before a big battle.
Resonance also lets you bring in characters from other Final Fantasy games to aid you in battle. (It’s a holdover from Resonance’s roots as a mobile title; the game is an “adaptation” of the first story arc of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, which was shut down in 2024.) As you move through Resonance, you’ll recruit “Visions” of characters like Final Fantasy VI’s Terra Branford or Final Fantasy VII’s Cloud Strife, and each of the game’s characters can “equip” one Vision to give them new moves in battle. Over time, while using a Vision with a Resonance character, you unlock more moves and abilities that you can use even when you don’t have that Vision equipped. It’s a clever system that offers a lot of possibilities for interesting builds, making the hunt for more Visions feel like more than just a way to get a hit of nostalgia.
But I’m already getting sucked into Resonance like I used to with classic Final Fantasy titles. At one point, as I was nodding my head to heart-pumping music during an intense boss fight on a moving train, I realized I was completely absorbed by the game in a way that only a Final Fantasy can pull off. The game’s old-school structure with modern improvements lets Square Enix have it both ways, as the old-school approach sits comfortably alongside a big-budget game like Final Fantasy XVI. The series has come a long way since the games that Resonance uses as inspiration, but it pulls in enough from newer titles that playing it feels like enjoying the best of both worlds.
Final Fantasy Resonance launches on October 22nd on Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S.

title: Antigravity just halved the price of its drone — by swapping its headset for wristwatch control
summary: Last year’s Antigravity A1 is the best beginner drone I’ve ever tried. I put a friend who’d never flown into its virtual cockpit and didn’t worry one bit. The A1’s also nice for people who’d prefer to think about flying rather than filming, because you can reframe its 360-degree footage after. Antig...
content:
Last year’s Antigravity A1 is the best beginner drone I’ve ever tried. I put a friend who’d never flown into its virtual cockpit and didn’t worry one bit. The A1’s also nice for people who’d prefer to think about flying rather than filming, because you can reframe its 360-degree footage after.
Antigravity just halved the price of its drone — by swapping its headset for wristwatch control
$800 now buys you a follow-me drone instead of an FPV flight experience.
But until today, that meant wearing the company’s FPV goggles and spending upwards of $1,599 on the complete set. Now, Antigravity is halving the price of entry to $799 in the US with a new “Follow Me” kit that replaces the original headset and motion controller with a wristwatch and ring instead.
The idea is that Antigravity can be your robot cameraman, automatically flying, following, and filming you with a minimum of gear.
I took the new kit for several test drives this fall, and I’m cautiously impressed.
Instead of powering on a headset and finding a safe place to sit while you block out the world, you can now pull a drone and a watch out of your bag, power them both on, hold a button to launch the drone from your hand, then walk or ride while the Antigravity A1 automatically films and follows you, dodging obstacles along the way.
You can even wave your arm like a magic wand to nudge the drone left, right, down, up, towards, or away while it’s filming. You get a swipeable preview of what the drone sees on the watch’s touchscreen, and can select various quickshots there or summon a couple of sliders (forward/backward, ascend/descend) to manually fly the A1 out of a jam. The ring doesn’t do anything you can’t already do with the watch; it’s just an extra button so you can launch and reposition it one-handed.
As I discovered after three crashes, the A1 is not yet intelligent enough to dodge everything or stay with me through thick and thin. I took it all around my neighborhood on a kick scooter, and you might want to be careful around power lines, thin branches, or the vertical guy wires holding utility poles in place.
There’s also a lot of rough edges I hope Antigravity will fix, like the sluggish experience swiping around the touchscreen, or how it won’t land on my hand without switching back to manual mode, or how I can’t get it to automatically start tracking and filming me — I always have to find myself on the watch screen, tap on myself, then tap another button to begin. I also ran into an issue where it wouldn’t follow me once I crested a high hill, because it thought it was flying at too high an altitude.
Most of all, I hope Antigravity will figure out how to keep the drone from drifting out into the street or over a neighbor’s fence when I tell it to follow right behind. It’s far smaller than me, so anywhere I go, I feel like it should fit!
But as you’ll hopefully see in a video I publish later today, it’s not bad at following me through a dense suburban environment! None of my crashes so far have crippled the drone, and I like how the watch automatically plays the last seconds of footage before a crash. It made it very easy to find the drone after.
Antigravity’s new full-coverage propeller guards can also help in case of impact; I saw the drone bounce right off one obstacle and keep flying. They’re included in the $799 set, though existing Antigravity A1 owners can buy the accessories too: it’s $340 for the watch and ring, and $40 for the guards, with a 20 percent discount for those who can prove they already own the aircraft.
Antigravity’s A1 is kind of like the folding Skydio I wish that company had made before it left consumers behind to serve industry instead. The self-flying Skydio 2 similarly had a few crashes in my tests and wouldn’t always stay in its lane. But I’ve long wanted a folding version I could easily stick in a bag, and the Antigravity A1 seems like the next best thing.

title: Powerful nor’easter churning up the East Coast
summary: A powerful nor’easter is churning up the East Coast and is on track to bring several days of heavy rain, flooding and strong winds. The storm is expected to stay far enough offshore that the heaviest rain will likely affect only the easternmost parts of the country. While the rain will stay mostly o...
content:
A powerful nor’easter is churning up the East Coast and is on track to bring several days of heavy rain, flooding and strong winds.
The storm is expected to stay far enough offshore that the heaviest rain will likely affect only the easternmost parts of the country. While the rain will stay mostly offshore, gusty winds and coastal flooding are still possible, especially across the Outer Banks.
Flood advisories are in place from the Jersey Shore to the Outer Banks for 1-2 feet of inundation from onshore winds.
The storm, still offshore, is intensifying. Coastline cities from New Jersey to Cape Hatteras can expect coastal flooding, beach erosion and gusty winds.
Rain and coastal flooding are expected to impact Cape Cod and Nantucket in the coming days. By Thursday, rough surf and rip currents will hit those areas.
The nor’easter could become a tropical storm but, if it does, it will only intensify as it continues east and away from the coast. It has a 40% chance of formation in two days, and 40% in seven days. If it develops, it will be named Josephine.
Winds will have the biggest impact, with 44 mph winds forecast in Nantucket. Virginia Beach could see 32 mph winds, and Cape Hatteras is expected to have 39 mph winds.

title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
summary: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains - Date: - October 20, 2026 - Source: - Florida State University - Summary: - A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the ...
content:
Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- Florida State University
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action. Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts and public preparedness.
- Share:
An updated hurricane forecast map is making it easier for people to identify areas threatened by storms, but new research reveals a concerning limitation. Even when people can recognize where hurricane watches are in effect, they may not feel more at risk or become more inclined to take precautions.
Researchers at Florida State University examined whether changes to the National Hurricane Center (NHC) forecast graphics improve public understanding of hurricane threats. The study involved faculty from the School of Communication within the College of Communication and Information and the Department of Geography.
The researchers evaluated an experimental graphic that expands the traditional hurricane forecast cone to include tropical storm and hurricane watches and warnings for inland areas. The familiar cone has historically placed greater emphasis on coastal regions, even though dangerous storm conditions can extend far from the shoreline.
The findings revealed mixed results. Although the revised graphic helped people without specialized weather knowledge recognize inland areas under hurricane or tropical storm watches, it did not significantly influence how dangerous they believed the storms would be or whether they intended to take protective measures. Participants also showed no improvement in identifying areas covered by storm warnings.
The updated format was developed by the NHC in 2024, and the findings were published in the American Meteorological Society journal Weather, Climate, and Society.
"The National Hurricane Center has made a number of thoughtful changes to improve how hurricane information is communicated," said Assistant Professor Elizabeth Ray, the study's lead author. "We had a simple question. Do those changes actually help people understand what the graphic is telling them about the risk they face?"
Why People Misunderstand Hurricane Forecast Maps
To investigate how the public interprets hurricane forecasts, the research team surveyed residents of Florida and Georgia. Participants were shown either the conventional hurricane cone graphic or the newer experimental version that includes additional information about inland storm threats.
People who saw the revised map were more successful at identifying locations under hurricane or tropical storm watches. However, that improvement in recognizing watch areas did not lead to greater concern about the potential danger or stronger intentions to take safety precautions.
The results also highlighted a persistent misunderstanding surrounding the familiar hurricane "cone of uncertainty." Many people incorrectly interpret the width of the cone as an indication of a storm's physical size, rather than understanding what the graphic is intended to communicate about the uncertainty in its projected track.
"For years, research has shown that people often mistake a wider cone for a bigger storm," Ray said. "Our findings suggest that even with an updated graphic, that misconception can be hard to shake."
Why Better Hurricane Warnings May Not Be Enough
The NHC introduced its expanded forecast graphic in 2024 to help people recognize that hurricane dangers are not limited to communities along the coast. Flooding, tornadoes, and destructive winds can threaten areas well inland, making it important for residents beyond coastal evacuation zones to understand their potential exposure.
By adding inland hurricane and tropical storm watches and warnings to the traditional forecast cone, the updated graphic provides a more complete picture of where dangerous conditions could develop.
However, the study suggests that adding useful information to a forecast does not automatically make people more aware of their personal risk or more likely to respond appropriately.
The researchers stressed that their findings do not call into question the quality of the NHC's weather predictions, which they consider highly accurate. Instead, the results underscore the difficulty of presenting complex meteorological information in a way that people can readily interpret and use when making safety decisions.
"Our question wasn't whether the science is good," said co-author Patrick Merle, professor and director of the School of Communication. "The science is excellent. The question is how we communicate that science so people who aren't meteorologists understand the risk they're facing.
If people find information credible but still don't understand it well enough to take protective action, then communication has fallen short. The goal is to empower people with information they can use to stay safe."
How to Better Understand Hurricane Risks
The findings point to the importance of looking beyond a single forecast image when preparing for a hurricane. Although the cone can provide valuable information about a storm's expected path, it cannot communicate every hazard that a particular community might experience.
The researchers recommend using hurricane forecast graphics alongside local weather predictions and detailed information about possible impacts. Understanding the specific threats to an area, as well as the protective steps residents should consider, can provide a more useful basis for making decisions.

content:
Milei atacó a Lula a días del balotaje con Bolsonaro en Brasil
El Presidente citó una entrevista de su par brasilero para acusarlo de “machirulo” y “zurdo ladrón”; la segunda vuelta es el 25 de octubre
- 2 minutos de lectura'
A pocos días del balotaje del 25 de octubre para definir la elección en Brasil, el presidente Javier Milei atacó a su par del país vecino, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, candidato que competirá contra el senador carioca Flávio Bolsonaro, a quien el libertario apoya. “Espero que su último truco de campaña sucia no incluya robarse la elección”, señaló el mandatario.
Milei citó un recorte de una entrevista a Lula en el que afirma que en Brasil no es viable trabajar seis días a la semana, a días de que el Parlamento sancionara la reducción de la jornada laboral de 48 a 40 horas, un logro del actual mandatario. “La mujer no puede trabajar seis días a la semana y descansar uno porque ese día tiene que limpiar la casa, lo que significa más trabajo”, afirmó Lula el lunes por la noche en SBT News. En esa charla, pretendía ejemplificar que en el país son en su mayoría las mujeres las que están a cargo de las tareas de cuidado.
Sacado de contexto, el Presidente argentino salió al ataque: “Los progres machirulos”. Luego sumó: “Después acusan de misóginos a todos sus oponentes...se les está cayendo la careta a estos delincuentes”.

content:
El descargo de Teresa Costantini tras las declaraciones de su exmarido, Eduardo Costantini: “Sin espacio para la mentira”
La cineasta emitió un comunicado en el que volvió a referirse al presunto pedido que le habría hecho el empresario sobre los restos de sus padres en el Jardín de Paz
- 3 minutos de lectura'
Continúa la disputa entre Teresa Costantini y su exmarido, Eduardo Costantini. Después de que se hiciera público el conflicto judicial por el uso del apellido que la directora de cine lleva desde hace décadas, y de que ella revelara recientemente que el fundador del MALBA le habría pedido que retirase los restos de sus padres del cementerio Jardín de Paz, el empresario catalogó las declaraciones de su exmujer como “una mentira absoluta” y aseguró que “el tema está terminado”. Ahora, la cineasta emitió un nuevo comunicado titulado “Sin espacio para la mentira”.
“Eduardo Costantini falta a la verdad cuando dice que ‘el tema está terminado’. En septiembre, la Justicia hizo lugar a la medida que presenté para que nadie pueda mover a mis padres del lugar donde descansan. Solicité esta medida amparada en mi derecho de copropietaria de esas parcelas, ya que las mismas no formaron parte del convenio de disolución de bienes en nuestro divorcio. Eduardo, ante la negativa de la Justicia, apeló el dictamen. Recién entonces, ante la sostenida insensatez, decidí hablar”, comenzó la cineasta en su descargo.
“Eduardo también falta a la verdad cuando dice que ya compró otras parcelas, como si eso hubiera resuelto la situación. Dicha compra la realizó en noviembre de 2025. El pedido para que retire a mis padres lo hizo por intermediarios el 1 de diciembre, cuando ya era propietario de las mismas. Omite decir, además, que todavía quedaba espacio libre en las parcelas de las que somos copropietarios. No le faltaba espacio”, explicó.
“Eduardo falta a la verdad cuando dice que la que miente soy yo. En la misma declaración en que lo niega, cuenta que ‘fue una idea’ y la justifica: ‘Si mañana me muero, no tengo lugar’. No se puede negar algo y explicarlo en la misma entrevista. Es de una profunda tristeza que ahora, expuesto, quiera hacer pasar esto como un ‘te dije me dijiste’. Todo está en la justicia documentado. Mis padres siguen donde están. Yo también”, concluyó.
“Es una mentira absoluta”
Consultado por LA NACION por la acusación de su exmujer, Costantini dijo ayer a este medio: “Yo tengo, desde hace mucho tiempo, tres parcelas en un cementerio muy conocido [Nota del editor: se refiere al Jardín de Paz]. Las tres están ocupadas, colmadas en su capacidad, por familiares. Entre otros, están los padres de Teresa y una de sus abuelas, que ya no son familiares míos. Yo no entro: si mañana me muero, no tengo lugar. Como la mayoría de los familiares están reducidos a cenizas, le pregunté a algunos de mis hijos si estaban dispuestos a hacer el traslado de las cenizas de sus abuelos y de su bisabuela a otro lugar dentro del cementerio. No es algo extraño, es algo que se hace comúnmente en los cementerios. Como mis hijos no estuvieron de acuerdo, jamás se avanzó con esta idea”.
Según las declaraciones de Eduardo Costantini, él nunca envió a nadie a hacerle ese pedido a Teresa, en tanto aseguró que no puede avanzar con el movimiento de los restos porque sería ilegal sin el permiso del familiar directo. Entonces, sostuvo: “El tema está terminado: compré otra parcela para seguir agrupando a los próximos muertos”.

title: Violencia en Francia: el gobierno de Macron ordena toques de queda y admite una “pérdida de control” en algunas ciudades
summary: Violencia en Francia: el gobierno de Macron ordena toques de queda y admite una “pérdida de control” en algunas ciudades El primer ministro instó a las autoridades locales a aplicar la medida en las zonas más afectadas por los saqueos; el ministro del Interior presentó su renuncia en medio de crecie...
content:
Violencia en Francia: el gobierno de Macron ordena toques de queda y admite una “pérdida de control” en algunas ciudades
El primer ministro instó a las autoridades locales a aplicar la medida en las zonas más afectadas por los saqueos; el ministro del Interior presentó su renuncia en medio de crecientes críticas
- 8 minutos de lectura'
PARÍS.– Tras dos días de saqueos e incendios, el gobierno francés comenzó a imponer este lunes toques de queda en varias ciudades del norte del país, en un intento por contener la ola de violencia que dejó miles de detenidos, cientos de policías heridos y al menos 3000 comercios afectados. Las primeras restricciones, que se extenderán durante las próximas dos noches, alcanzan sectores de Lille, Douai, Wattignies y Denain, mientras las autoridades evalúan medidas similares en otros puntos del territorio.
La decisión representa un giro en la respuesta del Ejecutivo frente a los disturbios que sacuden Francia desde el fin de semana. El primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu, había anunciado por la mañana la posibilidad de aplicar toques de queda “parciales y muy localizados”, una herramienta excepcional utilizada durante las revueltas de 2005 y 2023.
En medio de las críticas por la actuación policial, el ministro del Interior, Laurent Nuñez, presentó su dimisión, que fue rechazada de inmediato por el presidente Emmanuel Macron.
Francia despertó este lunes con las consecuencias de los días de disturbios y violencia. Vidrieras destrozadas, persianas metálicas arrancadas y el edificio del ayuntamiento de Limoges incendiado, con buena parte de su tejado derrumbado, reflejan la magnitud de los daños que dejaron las protestas contra el aumento del costo de vida.
Las escenas de caos en las principales ciudades francesas dieron la vuelta al mundo, mientras el gobierno intenta recuperar el control de las calles y evitar nuevos episodios de violencia.
Los primeros toques de queda
Las autoridades francesas anunciaron este lunes toques de queda para el lunes 19 y el martes 20 de octubre en varias ciudades del norte del país, las primeras restricciones de este tipo desde el estallido de los disturbios.
Según informó la oficina del primer ministro, Lille, Douai, Wattignies y Denain tendrán toques de queda entre las 20 y las 6 de la mañana durante las próximas dos noches, aunque las restricciones se limitarán a determinados sectores considerados vulnerables a nuevos episodios de violencia y saqueos. La medida busca proteger los comercios y evitar que se repitan los disturbios del fin de semana.
“El caos está muy localizado en los centros urbanos”, justificó el primer ministro Sébastien Lecornu, quien defendió la aplicación de restricciones “caso por caso”, en coordinación con las autoridades locales. Aunque no descartó declarar el estado de emergencia “si es necesario”, consideró que por el momento los toques de queda resultan más adecuados. En Denain, la alcaldesa limitó la medida municipal a determinadas zonas del centro y a los menores no acompañados.
En Marsella, las autoridades prohibieron las concentraciones este lunes entre el mediodía y las 20, mientras que en Guadalupe se impuso un toque de queda para menores en Pointe-à-Pitre y Les Abymes. París, Lyon y Marsella permanecen bajo especial vigilancia ante el riesgo de nuevos enfrentamientos, especialmente en los alrededores de Châtelet-Les Halles y la Plaza de la República, dos de los principales focos de tensión de la capital francesa.
Miles de detenidos y pérdidas millonarias
Para los comerciantes, a menudo arruinados en una sola noche, Matignon —sede del primer ministro— promete un dispositivo de paro parcial, cubierto al 100%, a partir del martes y un fondo de ayuda específico. La factura promete ser elevada: al menos 3000 comercios se han visto afectados, según el Gobierno, con daños valorados en cientos de millones de euros.
Una unidad de crisis reunida en Matignon debe gestionar el tema de los seguros y las consecuencias judiciales, y Lecornu se reunirá con los líderes de los partidos en los próximos días.
Hecho excepcional, contrariamente a otros episodios similares, esta vez la calma esperada nunca llegó. Al día siguiente de la jornada del sábado, que según el ministerio del Interior reunió a 550.000 manifestantes en las calles del país, grupos de saqueadores retomaron los pillajes el domingo en París, Lyon, Marsella y Nantes.
En la capital, alrededor de la plaza de la República, se quemaron bicicletas y los gases lacrimógenos volvieron a saturar el aire. Varios comercios fueron devastados y 108 personas detenidas, 66 de ellas durante la noche. En Le Mans, unos 300 manifestantes saquearon dos tiendas. En Lyon, la fiscalía contabiliza 199 detenciones desde el sábado. En Limoges, cerca de 7000 habitantes se congregaron ante las ruinas humeantes de su ayuntamiento.
El balance del fin de semana es abrumador: 2397 detenciones según el ministerio del Interior, 2331 arrestos (de los cuales el 70 % son adultos), según el ministro de Justicia Gérald Darmanin, y más de 600 policías y gendarmes heridos, según las autoridades.
Este lunes, además, manifestantes bloquearon el acceso al Museo del Louvre en apoyo al movimiento estudiantil y para denunciar “la represión policial” durante las protestas de los últimos días, lo cual impidió que el emblemático edificio abriera sus puertas a su hora habitual.
Des touristes venus visiter le musée du Louvre insultent et font des doigts d'honneur aux étudiants qui bloquent le musée depuis ce matin.#Louvre #Paris #17octobre #24octobre pic.twitter.com/YoH0cGgbie
— Luc Auffret (@LucAuffret) October 19, 2026
Autocrítica y nuevos métodos
Criticado por numerosos líderes políticos ya en campaña presidencial, el domingo por la noche Laurent Nuñez presentó su dimisión ante el jefe de Estado.
“Renuncié porque soy responsable de todo lo que ha pasado”, explicó este lunes en la radio France Inter el exprefecto de policía de París, reconociendo una “falta de anticipación” y una “pérdida de control”

title: Boca vuelve a Brasil por otra noche copera: la duda por Paredes y una noche decisiva en el Maracaná
summary: Encontrá resultados de fútbol en vivo, los próximos partidos, las tablas de posiciones, y todas las estadísticas de los principales torneos del mundo. Boca vuelve a Brasil por otra noche copera: la duda por Paredes y una noche decisiva en el Maracaná Este martes, desde las 21.30, buscará revertir el...
content:
Encontrá resultados de fútbol en vivo, los próximos partidos, las tablas de posiciones, y todas las estadísticas de los principales torneos del mundo.
Boca vuelve a Brasil por otra noche copera: la duda por Paredes y una noche decisiva en el Maracaná
Este martes, desde las 21.30, buscará revertir el 0-1 ante Vasco da Gama y avanzar a la final de la Sudamericana
- 5 minutos de lectura'
RÍO DE JANEIRO (Enviado especial).- Buena parte de la historia copera de Boca también se escribió en Brasil. No por casualidad es el club argentino que más series internacionales ganó en este país. Muchas veces incluso consiguió sus mejores resultados lejos de la Bombonera. Pero esta vez el desafío será distinto. Tendrá que revertir una llave que se complicó más de la cuenta: tras el 0-1 en casa, llega al Maracaná sin saber todavía si podrá contar con Leandro Paredes, su capitán y jugador emblema, que tendrá apenas 11 días de recuperación de un desgarro y será esperado hasta último momento.
Boca está a 90 minutos de una nueva final, como en 2023, cuando también en el Maracaná cayó ante Fluminense en la definición de la Copa Libertadores. Ahora el contexto es otro: se trata de la Sudamericana, pero la posibilidad de volver a disputar un título internacional volvió a encender la ilusión de sus hinchas. Para lograrlo, necesitará volver a encontrar esa mística copera que tantas veces mostró de este lado de la frontera.
El clima también es muy distinto al de aquella final. Río lleva varios días nublados, con algo de lluvia y máximas que no superan los 23 grados. Mientras tanto, la ciudad empezó a teñirse de azul y amarillo. Muchos hinchas llegaron durante el lunes y otros arribarán en micro pocas horas antes del encuentro.
En Copacabana, a unos 20 kilómetros de la concentración de Boca en Barra da Tijuca, cerca de mil simpatizantes se reunieron frente al Quiosque Buenos Aires, un tradicional bar de impronta argentina ubicado sobre la playa, donde realizaron un banderazo para acompañar al equipo de Rodolfo Arruabarrena y empezar a vivir la previa de un partido que puede marcar el pulso de la temporada.
La gran incógnita pasa por Paredes. Este lunes, en la práctica en el predio de Flamengo, el volante completó casi todos los ejercicios junto con sus compañeros, aunque sin demasiada intensidad.
El campeón del mundo se sometió a un tratamiento con plasma rico en plaquetas, similar al que realizó durante el Mundial, con la intención de acelerar la recuperación. Jugar, de todos modos, implica un riesgo. Boca todavía tiene por delante los clásicos con Independiente y River, la definición del Clausura, la pelea por la tabla anual y la Copa Argentina.
“Trataré de pensar en lo que más nos conviene deportivamente. Los tiempos no son los que pensábamos que íbamos a tener y tampoco me gusta arriesgar”, avisó Arruabarrena.
Si Paredes no llega para ser titular, Rodrigo Battaglia y Williams Alarcón son los candidatos a ocupar su lugar. Arriba hay otra duda: Sebastián Villa o Alan Velasco, dos jugadores que dejaron atrás sus lesiones; el que gane la pulseada acompañará en el ataque a Leonel Flores y Miguel Merentiel.
“Intentaremos hacer un partido largo, no vamos a salir a volvernos locos de entrada”, explicó el entrenador durante la rueda de prensa de este lunes en el hotel Windsor Marapendi.
Arruabarrena también buscará saldar una deuda internacional. En su etapa anterior ganó el campeonato local y la Copa Argentina de 2015, pero no llegó a disputar una final continental: en dos oportunidades quedó eliminado por River. Por la magnitud del cruce, decidió además que viajara todo el plantel, incluidos los lesionados Adam Bareiro, Tomás Belmonte y Agustín Marchesin, con Juan Román Riquelme como encargado de la delegación.
Vasco también llega con interrogantes. El lateral derecho Paulo Henrique sufrió un golpe en las costillas en la derrota 1-0 ante San Pablo del sábado, partido que el equipo carioca disputó con la mayoría de sus titulares, y desde entonces no pudo trabajar con normalidad. Además, Marino Hinestroza, que estuvo muy cerca de llegar a Boca en enero, entraría por Andrés Gómez, expulsado en la ida.
Se espera un Maracaná completo: Vasco agotó unas 70.000 localidades después del triunfo 1-0 en Buenos Aires, mientras que los hinchas visitantes tendrán 4.000 lugares.
Por la cantidad de público y los antecedentes, el partido fue clasificado como Bandera Roja según la Metodología de Avaliação de Risco em Estádios de Futebol (AREF). El operativo contará con unos 500 efectivos de distintas fuerzas, casi el doble de los que suelen trabajar en un encuentro habitual del Brasileirao. Además, el transporte público funcionará con horario extendido y habrá presencia policial reforzada en las estaciones de tren y subte.
También pesa lo ocurrido en 2023, cuando hubo incidentes entre hinchas de Boca y Fluminense en Copacabana durante la previa de la final de la Libertadores. Esta vez, las autoridades brasileñas prepararon un dispositivo especial para evitar cruces entre ambas parcialidades.
En el Maracaná, Boca apenas ganó una vez. Fue en 1998, cuando venció 2-0 a Flamengo por la Copa Mercosur; después acumuló cuatro derrotas.
Ahora llega en desventaja, pero también vuelve a un país en el que protagonizó varias de sus grandes gestas internacionales, obligado a sacar a relucir ese ADN copero que tantas veces demostró que a Boca jamás hay que darlo por muerto.
