title: Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
summary: Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen - Date: - October 20, 2026 - Source: - University of Manchester - Summary: - Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 m...
content:
Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- University of Manchester
- Summary:
- Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 million years ago. The exceptionally rare fossils reveal a creature unlike anything previously known, potentially a predator of smaller squid-like animals and a surprising survivor of a supposedly vanished family.
- Share:
Two extraordinarily rare fossils found in Wyoming have revealed a strange new species of squid relative that lived approximately 160 million years ago, during the Jurassic Period.
Named Wyoteuthis linsterorum, the prehistoric creature belonged to an extinct group of marine animals known as belemnites, which were related to modern squid and octopuses. What makes this species particularly remarkable is its unusually thick, barrel-shaped internal skeleton, earning it the distinction of being the "chunkiest" or "fattest" belemnite ever identified.
An international research team from the United States, United Kingdom, and New Zealand, including Dr. Dean Lomax, an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Manchester, detailed the discovery in the scientific journal Papers in Palaeontology.
An Unusually Thick Jurassic Squid Relative
Belemnites are among the most frequently discovered fossils in the world. They are best known for their distinctive, bullet-shaped internal skeletal structures, called rostra or guards, which are often the only parts of the animals that survive in the fossil record.
Wyoming's Sundance Formation, which preserves evidence of an ancient inland sea that once stretched across much of the western United States, has yielded millions of these fossils. According to Wyoming paleontologist and study coauthor Jessica Lippincott, they are commonly nicknamed "squid butts" in the region.
Most belemnite fossils from Wyoming have a narrow, bullet-shaped appearance, typically measuring between 5 and 10 centimeters in length and just 1 to 2 centimeters across. The newly identified species is dramatically different. Its rostrum measures approximately 10 centimeters long but reaches an extraordinary 6 centimeters in width, making it the thickest known example of its kind.
Scientists estimate that the living animal, including its arms, could have reached a total length of approximately 60 centimeters, or about two feet.
Rare Fossils Reveal a Surprising Evolutionary Secret
Wyoming paleontologist Bill Wahl, who has devoted much of his career to searching for fossils across the state, recognized that the unusual specimen deserved closer examination. He said the belemnite "stuck out like a sore thumb" compared with the countless others found in the region.
Wahl assembled an international team to investigate the fossils, bringing in specialists including belemnite expert Alexey Ippolitov, a PhD student now based at Victoria University of Wellington in New Zealand.
The researchers used computed tomography (CT) scanning to investigate the fossils' internal structures without damaging the specimens. These detailed scans revealed an unexpected connection to an ancient belemnite family that scientists had believed disappeared millions of years before this animal lived.
Ippolitov said he was "deeply surprised" to encounter such an unusual specimen from a group that has already been studied extensively. Belemnites have been the subject of paleontological research for more than 200 years, making the identification of such a radically different species especially remarkable.
The creature's unusual proportions may also offer clues about how it lived and hunted.
Ippolitov explains: "A possible explanation is that their relatively large size gave them an advantage when hunting co-occurring smaller belemnites of the genus Pachyteuthis. Modern squid, after all, are hardly picky when it comes to prey: they readily hunt not only other species of cephalopods, but sometimes even their own kind."
A Fossil Discovery Nearly 30 Years in the Making
Although the species has only now been formally described, its discovery began almost three decades ago.
The first known specimen was found in the late 1990s by Dr. Burkhard Pohl, founder of the Wyoming Dinosaur Center. While examining fossils, Pohl noticed a belemnite that was considerably larger than any he had previously encountered.
Despite its unusual appearance, the specimen remained unstudied in a museum collection drawer for many years.
A breakthrough came when fossil collector Cliff Linster discovered a second specimen near Ten Sleep, Wyoming. He donated the fossil to the Wyoming Dinosaur Center in 2019, providing researchers with another example of the mysterious animal.
With two specimens available for comparison, scientists finally had enough evidence to recognize and formally describe an entirely new species.
The genus name Wyoteuthis means "a squid from Wyoming," while the species name linsterorum recognizes Cliff Linster and his family for their contributions. Linster discovered one of the only two known examples and ensured it was available for scientific research.
Lippincott emphasized how extraordinary the discovery was, even for researchers familiar with Wyoming's abundant belemnite fossils.
"After spending years fossil hunting in Wyoming and collecting countless fossils of the common Pachyteuthis belemnites here in Wyoming, this one is unlike anything I have ever seen! It goes to show that we are still finding new species of fossils all the time, and people who rockhound or collect invertebrate fossils can also contribute to science."
Honoring a Fossil Hunter's Remarkable Legacy
Sadly, Cliff Linster passed away in June before the research was published. He had been aware that scientists were investigating his discovery and was enthusiastic about seeing the unusual fossil receive formal scientific recognition.

title: "Más del 80% de preñez en los primeros 27 días de servicio": claves para mejorar la eficiencia y la rentabilidad en rodeos comerciales de cría
summary: A través de la genética es posible mejorar variables productivas y acelerar los resultados en los rodeos comerciales de sistemas de cría, siempre acompañada de buen manejo, correcta nutrición y sanidad cuidada. Según Federico Hozbor, investigador del Grupo de Biotecnología de la Reproducción del INT...
content:
A través de la genética es posible mejorar variables productivas y acelerar los resultados en los rodeos comerciales de sistemas de cría, siempre acompañada de buen manejo, correcta nutrición y sanidad cuidada. Según Federico Hozbor, investigador del Grupo de Biotecnología de la Reproducción del INTA Balcarce, “las herramientas para alcanzar la eficiencia reproductiva ya están disponibles”. En un trabajo interdisciplinario realizado junto a su colega Hugo Nigro, especialista del INTA en manejo de rodeo de cría, demostraron cómo, con un programa de inseminación artificial a tiempo fijo (IATF) y repaso con toros a los 10 días de la inseminación, se alcanzó más del 80 % de preñez en los primeros 27 días de servicio.
Para lograrlo, indicaron, es fundamental que las vacas estén en balance energético positivo y una condición corporal no menor a 2,5 (escala de 1 a 5). Además, es necesario aplicar programas de IATF que permiten de manera simultánea concentrar los partos, aumentar el peso y la edad al destete (a fecha fija), introducir genética a bajo costo, y realizar un manejo mucho más racional de la alimentación y la sanidad del rodeo.
Para Pablo Veiga, veterinario especialista en reproducción bovina, “la genética es uno de los pilares de la producción ganadera eficiente”.
Entre los indicadores que definen la eficiencia de un rodeo, Veiga destacó “la cantidad de terneros producidos, el peso de cada ternero y los kilos de ternero producidos por hectárea”. De acuerdo con los datos del INTA, una mejora en el porcentaje de marcación puede generar diferencias económicas importantes en la facturación de un sistema de cría.
Dentro de las herramientas disponibles, la IATF apareció como una de las tecnologías de mayor impacto. “La IATF permite utilizar toros superiores probados, adelantar partos, concentrar la parición y producir animales más eficientes”, explicó Veiga.
Desde el INTA señalaron que el mercado de genética bovina mantiene una dinámica sostenida, con fuerte protagonismo de la inseminación artificial y una mayor demanda de semen y embriones. Según, informaron, en Argentina se comercializaron más de 8,3 millones de dosis de semen bovino, con predominio de razas para carne.
“Las biotecnologías de la reproducción permiten difundir genética mejoradora y reducir problemas sanitarios y de transporte”, remarcó Mariano Etcheverry, integrante de la Cámara Argentina de Biotecnología de la Reproducción e Inseminación Artificial (CABIA), y dijo que el mercado internacional sigue dominado por América del Norte y Europa, "aunque existen nichos para la genética carnicera argentina”.
Junto al ordenamiento reproductivo, esta técnica mejora indicadores productivos generales y acelera el progreso genético del rodeo. “Cuando se concentra la parición y se utilizan reproductores superiores, el resultado aparece rápidamente en los kilos producidos”, sostuvo Veiga.
Los especialistas, se refirieron también el avance de la genómica aplicada a bovinos de carne. Para Veiga, esta herramienta permite identificar genes asociados a características de importancia económica, como crecimiento, facilidad de parto y eficiencia de conversión. “La genómica mejora la precisión en la selección y permite tomar decisiones más objetivas”, indicó.
De todas maneras, el técnico aclaró que la genética por sí sola no resuelve los problemas productivos. “La genética no hace magia. Hay que tener controlados los demás factores involucrados en la producción”, advirtió.
En ese sentido, subrayó la importancia de sostener planes sanitarios, manejo reproductivo eficiente y registros productivos para que las herramientas genéticas expresen todo su potencial.
“El toro perfecto no existe, pero sí hay reproductores que pueden mejorar parámetros específicos alineados con los objetivos de cada rodeo”, concluyó Veiga.

title: Ingresó a la universidad a los 14 años, creó una empresa de manos robóticas y ahora su negocio está valuado en 3.000 millones de dólares
summary: Desde pequeño, Alex Zhou mostró interés por la robótica, inspirado por las series animadas que veía durante su infancia. Con el tiempo, esa curiosidad se transformó en una carrera tecnológica que lo llevó a fundar Linkerbot, una empresa china especializada en desarrollar manos robóticas capaces de r...
content:
Desde pequeño, Alex Zhou mostró interés por la robótica, inspirado por las series animadas que veía durante su infancia. Con el tiempo, esa curiosidad se transformó en una carrera tecnológica que lo llevó a fundar Linkerbot, una empresa china especializada en desarrollar manos robóticas capaces de reproducir movimientos humanos.
Su talento comenzó a destacarse a temprana edad. A los 14 años ingresó a la Universidad de Ciencia y Tecnología de Huazhong, en China, a través de un programa especial destinado a estudiantes con capacidades sobresalientes.
Años después, Zhou Yong, como se lo conoce legalmente en China, identificó uno de los principales desafíos de la robótica: crear manos artificiales que no solo puedan sujetar objetos, sino también manipular herramientas y realizar tareas que requieren precisión.
En 2023 fundó Linkerbot, una compañía que atrajo el interés de inversores y alcanzó una valoración de aproximadamente 3.000 millones de dólares después de una ronda de financiación de 400 millones.
De ingresar a la universidad a los 14 años a fundar una empresa millonaria
Después de completar sus estudios universitarios, Zhou comenzó a trabajar en Lenovo, una de las principales empresas tecnológicas de China. Durante dos años participó en el desarrollo de software para teléfonos inteligentes, una experiencia que le permitió adquirir conocimientos sobre la industria.
Posteriormente, decidió emprender y cofundó dos startups: una dedicada a los videojuegos y otra especializada en tecnología de conducción autónoma.
Ambas empresas fueron vendidas y Zhou utilizó parte del dinero obtenido para financiar un proyecto que había despertado su interés desde hacía años: el desarrollo de manos robóticas.
Su idea partía de una observación sobre las capacidades humanas. Aunque los robots pueden realizar movimientos repetitivos y levantar objetos pesados, reproducir la destreza de una mano humana continúa siendo un desafío tecnológico.
En 2023, Zhou fundó oficialmente Linkerbot con el objetivo de desarrollar dispositivos capaces de ejecutar movimientos más complejos y adaptarse a diferentes tareas.
La compañía comenzó a atraer inversiones y, tras recaudar aproximadamente 400 millones de dólares en abril, su valoración alcanzó los 3.000 millones de dólares. Esta cifra representa el valor estimado de la empresa, no las ganancias personales de su fundador.
Cómo funcionan las manos robóticas que desarrolla Linkerbot
Linkerbot fabrica distintos modelos de manos robóticas, con precios que oscilan entre los 996 y los 14.944 dólares, según sus características y capacidades.
Los dispositivos más sencillos pueden realizar movimientos básicos, como sujetar un teléfono inteligente. En cambio, los modelos más avanzados están diseñados para manipular objetos pequeños y utilizar herramientas que requieren mayor precisión, como pinzas.
Una de las características de la compañía es que fabrica internamente gran parte de sus componentes. Esto le permite controlar los procesos de producción, reducir costos y realizar modificaciones en sus diseños.
Según un informe del Instituto de Investigación Industrial de Gaogong, Linkerbot produjo aproximadamente 10.000 unidades en un año, una cifra que refleja su capacidad para fabricar estos dispositivos a escala comercial.
El mismo estudio ubicó a la empresa en el segundo puesto por volumen de envíos, detrás de Inspire Robots, una compañía fundada en 2016.
Sus productos se comercializan entre laboratorios de inteligencia artificial, universidades y empresas automotrices que utilizan manos robóticas para investigar y desarrollar nuevas aplicaciones.
De esta manera, Linkerbot busca pasar de la fabricación de prototipos experimentales a la producción de dispositivos destinados a distintos sectores industriales y científicos.
La inteligencia artificial que permite enseñar nuevas habilidades a los robots
Uno de los principales desafíos de la robótica no consiste únicamente en construir manos capaces de moverse, sino también en desarrollar sistemas que puedan controlar esos movimientos y adaptarlos a distintas situaciones.
Para avanzar en ese objetivo, Linkerbot creó LinkerSkillNet, una biblioteca de habilidades robóticas basada en inteligencia artificial.
La plataforma reúne más de 500 habilidades, entre ellas enhebrar agujas, cortar verduras y manipular objetos pequeños.
El propósito es que los robots puedan aprender diferentes tareas sin depender exclusivamente de una programación específica para cada movimiento.
Esta tecnología podría facilitar el desarrollo de máquinas capaces de realizar actividades en fábricas, laboratorios y otros entornos donde se requiere manipular objetos con precisión.
Zhou estableció una meta a largo plazo: producir un millón de manos robóticas capaces de aprender y ejecutar hasta un millón de habilidades diferentes.
Aunque se trata de un objetivo empresarial y no de una capacidad alcanzada actualmente, refleja la intención de ampliar las aplicaciones de la tecnología más allá de los procesos industriales tradicionales.
El próximo objetivo de Alex Zhou: fabricar prótesis robóticas por menos de 1.000 dólares
Además de desarrollar dispositivos para robots industriales, Zhou quiere aplicar los avances de Linkerbot a la fabricación de prótesis destinadas a personas que perdieron una mano.
Actualmente, las prótesis robóticas avanzadas pueden resultar costosas debido a la complejidad de sus componentes, sensores y sistemas de control.
El empresario considera que la experiencia adquirida en la fabricación de manos robóticas podría contribuir a reducir esos costos.
Su objetivo es desarrollar prótesis de mano con un precio inferior a los 1.000 dólares por unidad, una cifra que permitiría ofrecer una alternativa más económica frente a determinados dispositivos disponibles en el mercado.

title: Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag
summary: Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag - Published Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag said Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team and let me down" during the Dutchman's spell at Old Trafford. Portugal forward Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag took charge in the summer ...
content:
Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag
- Published
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag said Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team and let me down" during the Dutchman's spell at Old Trafford.
Portugal forward Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag took charge in the summer of 2022 but left in controversial circumstances a few months later.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag told The Athletic, external.
"I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."
Ten Hag had dropped Ronaldo for a Premier League game at Chelsea in October 2022 after he had refused to come on as a substitute against Tottenham three days earlier.
Ronaldo gave an interview in the November in which he said he felt "betrayed" by United, did not respect Ten Hag and was being forced out of the club prior to his departure being "mutually agreed".
- Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA 
  - Published15 hours ago
Ronaldo was 36 when he returned to Manchester United from Juventus in 2021, when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was manager.
Under Ten Hag, he scored just three goals in 16 outings before his exit during the 2022-23 campaign.
"It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted," added Ten Hag. "But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself.
"Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.
"He was telling the players, 'save your legs at the training'. I understand it when you are top fit - you have sessions you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels."
The publication of Ten Hag's interview comes as Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by the Portuguese Football Federation for leaving his country's international camp last month.
Ten Hag was sacked by Manchester United in October 2024, having won the Carabao Cup in 2023 and FA Cup in 2024.
On his time at Old Trafford, Ten Hag added he wanted to sign Frenkie de Jong, Harry Kane and Declan Rice, and was against the sale of Scott McTominay to Napoli in August 2024.
"I said for the first season, 'centre-half, there's a problem, centre-midfield, there is a problem, and especially I need a strategist, then we need goals'. And that was the biggest issue in all my three years: goals," said Ten Hag.

title: Scientists discover a way to kill dangerous gut bacteria without killing the good
summary: Scientists discover a way to kill dangerous gut bacteria without killing the good - Date: - October 20, 2026 - Source: - Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research - Summary: - Scientists have discovered a natural compound that targets dangerous C. difficile bacteria without wiping out the gut's benefi...
content:
Scientists discover a way to kill dangerous gut bacteria without killing the good
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a natural compound that targets dangerous C. difficile bacteria without wiping out the gut's beneficial microbes. Successful early tests suggest it could lead to a gentler, more effective treatment for stubborn intestinal infections that frequently return.
- Share:
A dangerous intestinal infection may soon have a more targeted treatment option. Scientists have identified a natural compound that can kill the bacteria responsible for severe gut infections while leaving much of the beneficial gut microbiome unharmed.
The bacterium Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile) is naturally found in the intestines of many people and generally causes no problems when present in small amounts. However, antibiotics that target a wide range of bacteria can upset the delicate balance of microorganisms in the gut. This disruption allows C. difficile to multiply rapidly, potentially causing severe intestinal inflammation that can become chronic.
C. difficile infections (CDI) are among the leading causes of diarrhea associated with antibiotic treatment. The bacteria produce toxins that can trigger dangerous and sometimes life-threatening inflammation in the intestines. Because these infections frequently return after treatment, scientists are searching for more effective ways to eliminate the pathogen without causing additional damage to the gut microbiome.
A team led by Prof. Rolf Müller, department head and scientific director at HIPS, has now identified a promising drug candidate that specifically targets C. difficile while preserving much of the gut's beneficial microbial community. HIPS is a site of the Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research (HZI) that operates in collaboration with Saarland University.
Natural Compound Targets Dangerous Gut Bacteria
The researchers found that argyrin B, a naturally occurring antibacterial substance, was highly effective against C. difficile in laboratory tests and experiments involving infected mice. Importantly, the compound showed little activity against the beneficial microorganisms that help maintain a healthy digestive system.
"We were able to show that the natural compound argyrin B is highly effective against CDI: both in laboratory experiments and in a mouse model of the infection, where it significantly reduces the bacterial load," says Dr. Jennifer Herrmann, senior scientist in the department "Microbial Natural Products" at HIPS. "An antibacterial target of the argyrins had previously been identified and characterized in the notorious hospital-acquired pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Now we have been able to show that argyrin B also acts on this target in C. difficile and exhibits particularly high efficacy in doing so. In contrast, the argyrins have virtually no effect on the beneficial microorganisms in our digestive tract. The gut microbiome could therefore be spared during treatment with argyrin and restored to a healthy state more quickly."
A Bacteria-Killing Substance Found in Soil
Argyrins were originally discovered in myxobacteria, microorganisms that inhabit soil. These bacteria produce natural substances that help them attack other microbes and use them as a source of food.
Although argyrin B has demonstrated promising antibacterial activity, researchers must also determine whether its pharmaceutical properties make it suitable for use as a medicine. That includes understanding how the compound behaves inside the body and whether it could cause unwanted effects.
One particularly encouraging finding emerged when the team examined what happens after mice receive argyrin B orally. Very little of the compound entered their bloodstream. Instead, most of it remained in the large intestine, where C. difficile infections occur.
By concentrating in the gut rather than circulating throughout the body, argyrin B could potentially reduce the risk of side effects affecting other organs. Together with its selective activity against C. difficile, this characteristic makes the compound a promising candidate for a treatment that may be better tolerated.
Could It Help Prevent Recurring Gut Infections?
One of the biggest challenges in treating C. difficile is its tendency to return. Patients who experience multiple relapses are often treated using fecal microbiota transfer (commonly known as a stool transplant). This procedure aims to restore a healthier balance of gut microorganisms, but it can be complicated to perform and unpleasant for patients.
A medication developed from argyrin could eventually provide another treatment option. By eliminating the harmful bacteria without extensively disrupting the rest of the microbiome, such a therapy might reduce the likelihood of further infections and relapses. That could also help some patients avoid the need for stool transplants.
More research is needed before argyrin B can be considered for clinical use. The scientists plan to investigate which dosage produces the strongest antibacterial effect and use additional experimental models to determine whether the compound can also combat recurring C. difficile infections.

Journal Reference:
- Sari Rasheed, Katrin Ehrhardt, Ahmed Mohamed Mostafa Abdrabou, Alexander Mellmann, Anna Lechleiter, Domen Pogorevc, Sabryna Junker, Lutz von Müller, Marius Vital, Jennifer Herrmann, Guntram A. Grassl, Markus Bischoff, Rolf Müller. Argyrin B exhibits potent therapeutic efficacy in a Clostridioides difficile-infection mouse model while preserving microbiota functionality. npj Antimicrobials and Resistance, 2026; 4 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s44259-026-00248-x

title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds
summary: A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study. The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payme...
content:
A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study.
The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems.
A two-year pilot managed by the UK-based charity Cool Earth gave 211 people in three communities in Peru’s Asháninka region six cash transfers of 1,032 Peruvian soles each – roughly equivalent to £2 a day – to spend as they wished.
Over the course of the trial, researchers found almost 90% of participants adopted environmentally beneficial practices, such as collective reforestation, restoration of critical water sources and reductions of forest burning.
They also noted a reduction in food insecurity, which can sometimes prompt forest people to start logging or become involved in environmental crimes. Households unable to afford nutritious food fell from 73% to 26%.
Another reported benefit was reduced migration, with the share of participants forced to leave their homes to find work falling from 43% to 18%. Researchers said this allowed more people to remain and protect the forest.
Dr Nick Langridge, a co-author of the report, said: “The findings suggest that when communities have greater security and autonomy, they are better able to protect the ecosystems they depend on.”
There is increasing recognition of the importance of Indigenous stewardship of the Amazon and other biomes that sequester carbon, shelter biodiversity and provide vital ecological services to the planet. But this role is increasingly difficult as Indigenous lands are threatened by miners, loggers, farmers and land grabbers, and as many of the young people of these often economically poor communities are exposed to the internet or lured away to wealthier cities.
How to sustain, encourage and reward Indigenous stewardship is a hot debate in the international aid and environmental community. Many previous payment schemes came with strings attached, such as the Brazilian government’s bolsa família, which has child education obligations, or bolsa verde, which has conservation activity requirements.
The authors of the new study say the project – which was drawn up with local women’s groups – is the first to offer an unconditional basic income to an Indigenous community in the Amazon.
The lead author, Dr Neil Howard, said: “All of this helps ethical conservation. The incentive to exploit or abandon land is diminished, and people are put front and centre with respect and dignity, which contrasts sharply with the colonial history of conservation and Indigenous policy.”
To boost the impact, the project delivered a voluntary “cash plus” complementary programme of community-led education on finance, conservation and climate change.
Other academics are more cautious about the environmental impacts of cash transfers, pointing out that similar studies elsewhere have found they can lead to an increase in deforestation as people use the extra cash to expand agriculture.
In some parts of the Amazon, cash payments are used to buy motorbikes and cars, which increases demand for more roads. There are also reports of Indigenous communities becoming more exposed to drugs when they visit cities to collect transfers.
The authors of the new report acknowledge that wider research is needed on the ecological impacts of unconditional basic income. Their two-year study was small, covering little over 500 hectares (1,235 acres) of forest. They did not measure changes in vegetation or soil quality, nor account for the influence of any separate projects that might have been affecting community behaviour.
Despite these limitations, they say the early results have excited the cash-for-conservation network of civil society organisations.
“Yes, this is an experimental pilot and and we could do with something much larger,” Howard said. “But this is very pioneering. My hope is that the trade-off between scale and innovation tips in this direction.”

title: Tlaxcala, feria con arraigo
summary: La importancia de este diminuto estado es inmensa, enorme en el mundo del toro, en la cultura de la tauromaquia y en la historia de México. Taurinamente hablando, es un mundo aparte; me encanta Tlaxcala porque tiene su ideología, sus costumbres, sus ídolos y sus códigos. Además, tiene una de las pla...
content:
La importancia de este diminuto estado es inmensa, enorme en el mundo del toro, en la cultura de la tauromaquia y en la historia de México. Taurinamente hablando, es un mundo aparte; me encanta Tlaxcala porque tiene su ideología, sus costumbres, sus ídolos y sus códigos. Además, tiene una de las plazas más bellas del país, si no es que la más, con el campanario del exconvento franciscano de Nuestra Señora de la Asunción —cuyo templo, del siglo XVI, es hoy la Catedral de Tlaxcala—, imponente, con privilegiada vista hacia el ruedo de la Ranchero Aguilar. Otra curiosidad es que es de los pocos campanarios que se encuentran separados del cuerpo del templo.
Precisamente ahí, en ese coqueto y torero rincón de la capital tlaxcalteca, este sábado dará comienzo su tradicional Feria del Día de Muertos con cuatro festejos de categoría.
La empresa Redondeles, que ha irrumpido con fuerza en el panorama taurino nacional, es la encargada de organizar el serial y lo ha hecho con talento, buen gusto y afición.
Vivir una corrida de toros en Tlaxcala capital es una experiencia distinta que comienza desde la belleza arquitectónica del zócalo, su jardín, los cuatro costados que lo rodean, los cafés y restaurantes aledaños, el hotel de los toreros y ese ambiente de tarde de toros único que ilusiona y nos hace viajar kilómetros.
El cartel inaugural tiene grandes alicientes para recorrer este sábado 24 los 120 kilómetros que separan la CDMX de Tlaxcala. Debido al ayuno taurino capitalino, consecuencia de la absurda imposición reglamentaria provocada por la incapaz, resentida y poco seria Clara Brugada y la parvada de los verdes encabezada por Chuchito Sesma, una vergüenza nacional, un gran número de capitalinos haremos el viaje a Tlaxcala.
Encabeza el cartel José Luis Angelino, torero tlaxcalteca de enorme capacidad y oficio, quien dice adiós a la profesión en activo, pero no a la tauromaquia. Debutó como novillero en Huamantla en 1996, con el debut empresarial de Promotoro —¡qué tiempos aquellos!—, así que para mí será un gusto estar ahí en el adiós de un muy buen torero, extraordinario tentador, buen hombre y mejor taurino.
Comparte cartel ni más ni menos que con Diego Silveti, torero de dinastía que está en su mejor momento, asolerado, con reposo y disfrutando cada tarde y cada toro. Cierra cartel el sevillano Juan Ortega, un torero fino, capaz de detener el tiempo y cuyas maneras evocan otras épocas: sus andares, su vestir y, sobre todo, su estética y su valor para hacer el toreo que gusta en México.
Por si fuera poco, se jugará un encierro bien presentado de la ganadería de Las Huertas, propiedad de Rodrigo Barroso, hombre apasionado de la bravura, del toro y del linaje que le precede como ganadero, así que todo pinta para que vivamos un sábado inolvidable.
Para rematar, el domingo nos regresamos por Texcoco y hacemos escala obligada en Cinco Villas, que presenta la Corrida del Arte con Juan Ortega, quien se ha enamorado de México, de su afición, de su toro y de sus formas. Alternará con Luis David Adame, que pasa por un gran momento, y con Arturo Gilio, en quien será interesante ver la evolución que ha conseguido al estar bajo la tutela artística de un gran torero como José Antonio Carretero. Este par de jóvenes tiene gran capacidad y estoy seguro de que será un agarrón de escándalo. El encierro de Montecristo, propiedad de don Germán Mercado, es garantía para un domingo pletórico de emociones.
Hasta el 14 de noviembre, Tlaxcala acapara gran parte de la atención taurina con carteles rematados de figuras nacionales y extranjeras alternando con toreros jóvenes. Llenemos las plazas, así defendemos nuestra libertad.

title: Spotify launches paid podcast memberships with perks beyond bonus content
summary: Spotify on Tuesday launched paid memberships, a new way for podcasters to make money from their biggest fans beyond paywalled bonus episodes. Creators can decide which perks to offer listeners, which could be bonus audio or video, fewer ads, early access to shows, or some combination of these. The s...
content:
Spotify on Tuesday launched paid memberships, a new way for podcasters to make money from their biggest fans beyond paywalled bonus episodes. Creators can decide which perks to offer listeners, which could be bonus audio or video, fewer ads, early access to shows, or some combination of these.
The streaming service first previewed the idea at its Investor Day in May, where it also introduced AI capabilities that let listeners ask questions about what they’re listening to or watching and debuted new tools for managing creator sponsorships.
As the company explained at the time, memberships would help to “create a natural path to go deeper, unlocking new and exclusive experiences for fans and new revenue opportunities for creators.”
The feature is now rolling out to 34 markets globally, including the U.S.
The launch is the latest example of Spotify’s effort to make its platform more attractive to podcast creators, particularly as it moves further into the video space to compete with YouTube. Though podcasters have long been able to monetize through ads, the new memberships could entice more fans to support creators by offering more than just an occasional bonus episode.
Creators keep 90% of the membership revenue and can package their benefits across multiple tiers and pricing options to appeal to fans at different levels of commitment. To qualify, podcasters must host their shows on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone, have at least 100 consumption hours, 100 listeners or viewers, and at least three published episodes.
Fans will see memberships promoted on the show’s Spotify page, where they can subscribe, pay, and immediately access the exclusive content. (The company tells us that memberships will be purchased on the web, not through in-app purchases).
A handful of shows will offer memberships at launch, including “The Adam Friedland Show,” “Making Sense with Sam Harris,” “Shawn Ryan Show,” “The Sculpt Society,” “Two Hot Takes,” as well as YMH Studios, which is bringing memberships to 12 shows across its network.
Memberships join other Spotify monetization tools, including advertising and the Spotify Partner Program, as well as features that help creators grow their audience, like promotions, free trials, and analytics. Soon, Spotify says creators will be able to offer fans membership badges and welcome clips, too.

title: Oura adds new fitness metrics to show how workouts impact your body
summary: As competition in the smart ring market escalates, Oura is introducing two new features to give people more insight into their workouts and how they impact their bodies. The company announced on Tuesday it’s rolling out Cardio Effort and VO₂ max metrics to expand workout tracking beyond exercise dur...
content:
As competition in the smart ring market escalates, Oura is introducing two new features to give people more insight into their workouts and how they impact their bodies. The company announced on Tuesday it’s rolling out Cardio Effort and VO₂ max metrics to expand workout tracking beyond exercise duration and heart rate zones.
While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, rivals like RingConn and Ultrahuman are emerging to dethrone it, putting pressure on the company to keep innovating. By launching more advanced workout metrics, Oura is looking to differentiate itself from competitors.
With Cardio Effort, users will be able to see how much a workout taxes their cardiovascular system. This measurement is aggregated over the week relative to each user’s individual baseline to provide more insights. Oura explained that this metric shifts users’ focus from “How many minutes did I move?” to “Am I maintaining my fitness, building it, or overdoing it?”
Since Cardio Effort accounts for both intensity and duration, a shorter, more intense workout can yield a similar score to a longer, less intense one, the company says.
Oura notes that the metric has two components: Workout Cardio Effort and Weekly Cardio Effort. The first metric evaluates the impact of an individual workout, while the latter aggregates effort into a weekly total, categorized as “Light,” “Fair,” “Maintaining,” “Building,” or “Reaching.”
Oura measures elevated heart rate relative to each member’s long-term resting heart rate, avoiding the variability associated with maximum-heart-rate estimates. Weekly effort levels are then determined using personalized ranges based on recent activity patterns.
Cardio Effort is rolling out to Oura Ring Gen3 and later models.
As for VO₂ max, the metric shows how workouts contribute to long-term fitness. It measures how effectively the heart, lungs, and muscles work together to deliver and use oxygen during exercise. Previously, measuring VO₂ max typically required a lab test or a six-minute walking test. Oura can now estimate it passively using GPS-enabled workouts.
After completing five qualifying activities, users receive an initial VO2 Max estimate. Within the My Health Heart Hub, they can view their current VO2 Max estimate in ml/kg/min, their fitness category (Low, Fair, High, or Peak), how their estimate has changed over time, and when it was last updated. Users also receive insights highlighting meaningful changes in their VO2 Max or indicating when their estimate remains consistent.
VO₂ Max is launching in Oura Labs, the company’s hub for experimental features, for members with Gen3 and newer Oura Ring devices.
Oura says these two new features are designed to work together to show users how hard they’re working and how that effort is adding up over time.

title: Spotify’s new podcast memberships let you pay for extra perks
summary: Spotify is enabling podcast creators to earn more money through the platform by providing their fans with a way to pay to access exclusive content. First announced in May, the new Memberships subscription feature is starting to roll out in 34 regions today, allowing podcasters to offer perks includi...
content:
Spotify is enabling podcast creators to earn more money through the platform by providing their fans with a way to pay to access exclusive content. First announced in May, the new Memberships subscription feature is starting to roll out in 34 regions today, allowing podcasters to offer perks including additional content, early access, bonus episodes, and reduced ads behind a paywall.
Spotify’s new podcast memberships let you pay for extra perks
Creators can offer bonus content, early access, fewer ads, and more.
Users can find Memberships on a podcast’s Spotify page, with the ability to subscribe, pay, and access the exclusive benefits “in just a few taps,” according to Spotify. Podcast creators can set their pricing options and bundle benefits across multiple subscription tiers, and keep 90 percent of membership revenue. Spotify is providing podcasters with tools to analyze and build their Memberships audience, including targeted promotions and free trial offers, alongside community engagement features like member badges, welcome clips, and more.
That makes this more like a Patreon-style membership system in which fans can choose to give additional support to their favorite creators, and is distinct from the podcast subscription feature that Spotify introduced in 2021. Podcasters can utilize Memberships alongside other Spotify revenue streams, including ads and the Spotify Partner Program.
To qualify for Memberships, shows must be hosted on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone, and have at least 100 consumption hours, 100 listeners or viewers, and three published episodes. Spotify is also making it easy for podcasters who manage their subscriptions on other services to try Memberships, allowing them to bring their paywalled content to Spotify via its Open Access feature.

title: Shark kills woman swimming off popular beach in South Africa
summary: Shark kills woman swimming off popular beach in South Africa A woman died after being mauled by a shark while swimming off a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast on Tuesday, witnesses and authorities said. Fatal shark attacks are uncommon worldwide but South Africa has a history of dea...
content:
Shark kills woman swimming off popular beach in South Africa
A woman died after being mauled by a shark while swimming off a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast on Tuesday, witnesses and authorities said.
Fatal shark attacks are uncommon worldwide but South Africa has a history of deadly encounters along its long coastline.
Tuesday's attack was at Orient Beach in KuGompo City, previously known as East London.
Police said they were called to the scene at around 7:00 am local time, where they found the body of a 65-year-old woman with "open wounds."
Local media reported the woman was a regular swimmer and had been swimming with a group when the attack occurred. A local community group said other swimmers had spotted a shark's tail and fin. The group said the woman sustained "severe injuries to the right side of her arm and leg."
After the attack, the municipality closed nearby beaches and urged the public to stay out of the water.
"It has been confirmed that a shark attack occurred at Orient Beach this morning, and this resulted in a tragic incident," the city said in a statement.
The incident comes about one month after a man was killed by a shark in front of beachgoers as he swam off a Western Australian city shore.
There were 65 unprovoked shark bites worldwide in 2025, up from 47 the previous year, including nine fatalities, according to the University of Florida's International Shark Attack File. There was one unprovoked attack in South Africa last year, which was fatal. By contrast, there were 25 unprovoked attacks in the U.S. (one fatal) and 21 unprovoked attacks in Australia (five fatal).
In 2022, there were two fatal shark attacks in South Africa, including a 39-year-old woman who was on vacation with her husband and young child when she was killed.
 Researchers say encounters can be influenced by a range of factors, including growing coastal populations, increased use of marine waters, environmental changes and shifts in the distribution of sharks and their prey.

title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
summary: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable - Date: - October 20, 2026 - Source: - Association for Psychological Science - Summary: - The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering deta...
content:
Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- Association for Psychological Science
- Summary:
- The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture. Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations.
- Share:
Growing older is often associated with memory loss and declining mental abilities. However, scientists are questioning whether these changes tell the whole story. Rather than simply becoming less capable, the brain may be adapting to a new stage of life in which accumulated knowledge, wisdom, and understanding become more important than remembering every detail.
Researchers at the University of Arizona have proposed a different way of understanding cognitive aging. Drawing on findings from molecular biology and brain imaging, they suggest that the changes occurring in older brains may reflect a natural stage of human development rather than deterioration alone. Their work, published in Perspectives on Psychological Science, offers a new perspective on why thinking and memory change with age.
The researchers call their proposed explanation the adaptive aging hypothesis. It suggests that the brain gradually adjusts its priorities to make better use of a lifetime of accumulated experience. This could help explain why older adults often have valuable strengths in teaching, mentoring, storytelling, and passing knowledge to younger generations.
"If we look at normative aging as a story of just decline, we are really missing the boat," said study coauthor Fabian-Xosé Fernandez, an associate professor of cognition and neural systems at the University of Arizona. "The older brain is optimized for different things than the younger brain, predominantly the sharing of stored expertise and social relationships."
How the Brain Shifts From Memory to Meaning
Two brain regions play important roles in how people remember and interpret their experiences. The hippocampus helps preserve specific information about events, including their details and circumstances. The frontal cortex, meanwhile, is more involved in extracting broader meaning, recognizing patterns, and understanding the central message of an experience, sometimes called its "gist."
According to the researchers, the balance between these systems changes during healthy aging. As people grow older, the brain tends to place less emphasis on activity in the hippocampus and rely more on the frontal cortex. This shift may allow the brain to focus more on interpreting information through existing knowledge rather than recording every new experience in precise detail.
"The fact that you see this across people and animal models suggests there is an evolutionary driving force," Fernandez said. "One could argue you are developing your entire life, and development occurs in lockstep with the needs of your brain. When you're younger, the hippocampus turns on because you don't have a knowledge base or know how the world works. A kid absorbs information like a sponge because they are building an archive of information. In early life, the balance is tilted toward recollecting declarative memories with precision, detail, and context."
Young brains need to gather enormous amounts of new information because they are still building a foundation for understanding the world. By later adulthood, however, people have already developed extensive stores of memories, concepts, and experiences. Connecting new information to what they already know may become more useful than retaining every individual detail.
The researchers suggest that this changing balance reflects a shift in how the brain processes experience. Instead of concentrating primarily on collecting detailed memories, it increasingly emphasizes understanding relationships, identifying underlying meaning, and applying previously acquired knowledge.
Why Evolution May Favor Wisdom in Older Adults
Evidence of similar changes in animal models raises the possibility that this transition has an evolutionary explanation. Fernandez suggests that the aging brain may be adapting to help individuals preserve and share the knowledge they have acquired throughout their lives.
From this perspective, the ability to draw on decades of experience could be especially valuable for making judgments, guiding others, and transferring important information between generations. Older adults may therefore play a distinct role in supporting younger people through mentorship, teaching, and storytelling.
"Given those goals, it makes sense that you aren't interested in nitty-gritty details," Fernandez said. "You are interested in safeguarding the vast knowledge you already have. Evolution may be saying that if you make it long enough, there's a need to transmit this information, so we put into motion biological changes that enforce and protect your semantic and autobiographical memories."
Under this hypothesis, changes in memory and thinking are not necessarily signs that the brain is functioning less effectively. They may instead reflect a different set of priorities, with greater emphasis on preserving meaningful knowledge and using it to understand new situations.
Why Healthy Brain Aging Is Different From Alzheimer's
The adaptive aging hypothesis could also provide scientists with another way to examine the differences between normal cognitive aging and Alzheimer's disease.
Although both involve changes in memory, Fernandez emphasizes that Alzheimer's should not be understood as ordinary aging taken to an extreme. The biological processes involved are fundamentally different.

title: El diagnóstico que el IMSS ya debía tener
summary: El 12 de octubre, con las protestas de trabajadores extendiéndose por el país, el director general del IMSS, Zoé Robledo, anunció que su equipo recorrería “piso por piso” 277 hospitales para preguntar al personal qué hace falta. Al día siguiente, la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum pidió “un verdadero d...
content:
El 12 de octubre, con las protestas de trabajadores extendiéndose por el país, el director general del IMSS, Zoé Robledo, anunció que su equipo recorrería “piso por piso” 277 hospitales para preguntar al personal qué hace falta. Al día siguiente, la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum pidió “un verdadero diagnóstico para poder atender lo que no está resuelto”. La respuesta institucional es una consulta de pasillo, y llega cuando Robledo suma siete años y cinco meses en el cargo, bajo dos presidentes.
Escuchar a los trabajadores nunca sobra. El problema es otro. Las normas del propio Instituto lo obligan a saber, casi al día, qué medicamento falta en cada servicio. Para las unidades médicas del primer nivel de atención del IMSS, el procedimiento 2200-003-001 ordena calcular el consumo promedio mensual de cada clave, medir cada mes el porcentaje de surtimiento por servicio e informar a diario qué claves hay y cuáles no.
Para los hospitales y Unidades Médicas de Alta Especialidad (UMAE) el procedimiento 1832-003-004 establece obligaciones equivalentes. Para el equipamiento médico, la norma 2000-001-012 (Norma para la solicitud de equipo médico en el IMSS) establece un sistema electrónico, el PREI-PROFORMA, como único canal de solicitud, con prioridades por unidad que las Delegaciones (OOAD) y las UMAE están obligadas a mantenerla actualizada. Y la Ley Federal de las Entidades Paraestatales obliga al titular a recabar información que refleje el estado de la institución. La información, en suma, debería existir sin necesidad de recorrer pasillos.
De hecho, buena parte ya existía. La Encuesta de Calidad 2025 del IMSS, con 17 mil 82 cuestionarios levantados en octubre y noviembre del año pasado, encontró que 20.3 por ciento de quienes reciben receta no la obtiene completa, y que 94.8 por ciento de esos faltantes se explica por falta de inventario. Tres de cada diez afectados compran el medicamento con su dinero. Una de cada cuatro cirugías no se realiza en la fecha programada, y 63 por ciento de esas suspensiones ocurre porque el Instituto no tenía el recurso comprometido.
Los indicadores internos de desempeño cuentan lo mismo. En el avance de la evaluación del desempeño de agosto de 2026, (documento interno y preliminar de la Dirección de Prestaciones Médicas), el promedio de las 35 representaciones estatales fue de 62.7 puntos sobre 100. Ninguna alcanzó el nivel esperado y 12 quedaron en desempeño bajo.
En las 25 UMAE el promedio fue de 75 puntos: ninguna llegó a la meta de 90 y 18 están en rango bajo. El área de observación de urgencias del hospital Magdalena Salinas opera al doble de su capacidad. En el hospital de especialidades de Ciudad Obregón se suspende el 14.6 por ciento de las cirugías programadas, casi el triple de la meta de 5 por ciento. En el de Mérida, apenas 26 por ciento de los pacientes recibe su cirugía electiva en menos de 20 días hábiles.
La CNDH completa el cuadro. El IMSS ha sido la autoridad federal con más expedientes de queja en cada año desde 2020. En 2025 sumó 5 mil 210 y acumula 515 recomendaciones en trámite.
Con ese acervo, la consulta difícilmente descubrirá algo nuevo. Al 16 de octubre, según cifras del IMSS difundidas en medios, había 7 mil 474 necesidades registradas, pero solo se detallaron los principales rubros, que suman 2 mil 630. Las 385 “necesidades de personal” no equivalen a 385 plazas, y de medicamentos no se publicó cifra alguna.
Conviene no simplificar: la anulación de la licitación consolidada 2025-2026 por sobreprecios y el incumplimiento de proveedores agravaron la crisis desde fuera de los hospitales. Pero nada de esto explica por qué una institución obligada a medirse cada mes necesita preguntar en los pasillos lo que sus propios sistemas deberían mostrar en pantalla.
El dinero tampoco resuelve la ecuación por sí solo. El proyecto de presupuesto 2027 asigna al IMSS cerca de 1.8 billones de pesos, 9.8 por ciento más que este año, y la Comisión de Seguridad Social de San Lázaro pide mil millones adicionales para prestaciones e infraestructura. Si ese monto se destinara íntegro a salarios, alcanzaría para subir el sueldo tabular alrededor de 1.7 por ciento con cargas patronales. Y si las pensiones del régimen de jubilaciones de los propios trabajadores del IMSS se ajustan con los aumentos de los activos, como describe la Auditoría Superior, el margen caería a 0.4 por ciento (cálculos propios con base en el informe de servicios personales del IMSS).
La Presidenta hizo lo que corresponde a quien encabeza el Ejecutivo: pedir un diagnóstico verdadero a quien tiene la responsabilidad directa de la institución. Si ese diagnóstico no estaba sobre su escritorio, la pregunta no es para ella. Es para la cadena que debía hacerlo llegar.
Más útil que otro recorrido sería publicar lo que los sistemas del IMSS ya producen: las claves en desabasto por unidad, el surtimiento real, las prioridades de equipamiento médico, las plazas vacantes por hospital. Con esos datos, las mesas con el sindicato y el presupuesto de 2027 tendrían una base firme. Sin ellos, el piso por piso corre el riesgo de quedarse en eso, un recorrido de pasillos.

title: “No alcanzaron el nivel”: declaran desiertos tres concursos que buscaban director para museos históricos nacionales
summary: “No alcanzaron el nivel”: declaran desiertos tres concursos que buscaban director para museos históricos nacionales Los candidatos no pudieron acreditar conocimientos suficientes para avanzar en el proceso de selección de los cargos en el Museo Histórico Nacional, el del Cabildo y el José A. Terry, ...
content:
“No alcanzaron el nivel”: declaran desiertos tres concursos que buscaban director para museos históricos nacionales
Los candidatos no pudieron acreditar conocimientos suficientes para avanzar en el proceso de selección de los cargos en el Museo Histórico Nacional, el del Cabildo y el José A. Terry, en Jujuy; volverán a convocarse
- 3 minutos de lectura'
La primera etapa de la convocatoria para ocupar cargos de dirección en cinco museos no fue un éxito. Tres de los cinco concursos públicos y abiertos de museos nacionales fueron declarados desiertos esta semana por el jurado conformado por representantes del Fondo Nacional de las Artes, la Secretaría de Cultura, la Secretaría de Transformación del Estado y Función Pública y un experto externo de la función pública: Tulio Andreussi Guzmán, María Paula Zingoni, Karen Valeria Vázquez y Héctor Ricardo Cicerchia, respectivamente. Se trata del Museo Histórico Nacional (MHN, interinamente a cargo de uno los jurados, Zingoni), el Museo Histórico Nacional del Cabildo y de la Revolución de Mayo y el Museo Regional de Pintura José A. Terry, en Jujuy. En el caso del MHN, ni siquiera se llegó a conformar una terna.
En calidad de veedoras, participaron Paula Aguirre, en representación de la Unión del Personal Civil de la Nación; Julia Pirani, en representación de la Asociación de Trabajadores del Estado, y María del Pilar Mayoral, en representación de la Subsecretaría de Derechos Humanos. María Belén Valenzuela ofició de coordinadora concursal.
Según informaron desde la Secretaría de Cultura y la Secretaría de Empleo Público, los candidatos “fueron cayendo en etapas administrativas y de evaluación” y no pudieron acreditar conocimientos y publicaciones suficientes para alcanzar el puntaje necesario. “No alcanzaron el nivel buscado”, resumieron.
El proceso de selección de directores del Museo Casa de Rogelio Yrurtia y del Museo Casa Ricardo Rojas continúa abierto.
“La convocatoria a concurso de los cargos directivos de los museos nacionales responde al compromiso de garantizar procesos basados en el mérito, la idoneidad y la igualdad de oportunidades -señalaron desde la Secretaría de Cultura a LA NACION-. El objetivo es seleccionar a los candidatos más capacitados para asumir cada responsabilidad y desarrollar proyectos de gestión sólidos y sostenibles. Que un cargo pueda quedar desierto en alguna de las instancias no constituye un fracaso, sino una posibilidad contemplada en el propio mecanismo, que prioriza la calidad de los perfiles seleccionados por encima de la cobertura automática de las vacantes”.
Especialistas consultados por LA NACION opinaron que pocos expertos en historia, arte o gestión cultural dejarían su cargo en universidades o en el Conicet para pasar a ganar tres millones y medio de pesos por mes y quedar sujeto a los antojos de los funcionarios de turno.
En la Subsecretaría de Patrimonio, a cargo de Liliana Barela, se decidió que los tres museos se sumarán a la siguiente convocatoria, que estaba prevista para otras nueve instituciones; ahora, serán doce. Se estima que la segunda etapa de concursos se lance antes de fin de año y se extienda a los primeros meses de 2027, para darle mayor difusión.
Además de los museos mencionados, entonces, se concursarán los cargos de dirección del Museo Histórico Sarmiento, el Museo Roca, el Museo de la Estancia Jesuítica de Alta Gracia y Casa de Virrey Liniers, la Casa Histórica de Tucumán, el Museo Histórico del Norte (Cabildo de Salta, Museo Presidente José Evaristo Uriburu y Museo Posta de Yatasto), el Museo Nacional del Grabado, el Museo Nacional de Arte Decorativo, el Instituto Nacional de Antropología y Pensamiento Latinoamericano y el Instituto Nacional de Musicología “Carlos Vega”.

title: Posibles causas de la crisis social europea y riesgo de que ocurra en México
summary: Europa había sido ejemplo de estabilidad y progreso en las pasadas décadas, pero en los últimos años, y sobre todo en los meses recientes, predomina un importante descontento social, lo que culmina en un estado social, principalmente en Francia, pero también ocurre en Italia, en España y hay brotes ...
content:
Europa había sido ejemplo de estabilidad y progreso en las pasadas décadas, pero en los últimos años, y sobre todo en los meses recientes, predomina un importante descontento social, lo que culmina en un estado social, principalmente en Francia, pero también ocurre en Italia, en España y hay brotes de conflicto social en los Países Bajos y en el Reino Unido. Diversos grupos sociales, de distintas edades e ideologías hacen frente común en su enfrentamiento contra los diversos gobiernos. Esta situación amenaza replicarse en otros países en las siguientes semanas, incluso en Latinoamérica, sin descartar a México.
Las causas originales para entender estos conflictos pueden ser muy diversas, como es la demanda por más recursos para la educación o apoyo a los sectores más necesitados, mayores facilidades para adquirir vivienda o incrementos en los sueldos y salarios. En general destacan los programas de apoyo a la población, como son el servicio médico gratuito o de bajo costo, así como el seguro al desempleo, lograr educación pública de calidad y gratuita y varios más.
Es decir, la principal demanda de la sociedad es que se proporcionen más recursos a los distintos programas que otorgan los gobiernos, es decir que aumente el gasto público. Sin embargo, lo frecuente es que en su origen se propongan y se aprueben estos programas sin un esquema claro de cómo se van a fondear, es decir, de dónde se van a obtener los suficientes recursos para que operen en el presente y en el futuro.
Como los recursos públicos no son suficientes para todos los programas públicos, lo que ha sucedido es que los gobiernos han incrementado su deuda, es decir, esperan que los siguientes gobiernos y generaciones absorban este costo. Por ejemplo, la deuda del gobierno en Japón representa el 250% de su PIB, en Italia es el 135%, en Grecia la deuda equivale al 146% del PIB, en España el 122%, mientras en el Reino Unido es el 93%. El caso de Estados Unidos es diferente porque su gobierno puede imprimir su propia moneda para pagar su deuda, pero la misma ya equivale al 122% de su PIB. El caso más elevado es el de Venezuela, donde la deuda ya equivale al 309% de su PIB.
Este mayor endeudamiento tenía un reducido impacto en el total del gasto público por las bajas tasas de interés, cercanas al 1% mensual a finales de la década pasada. Sin embargo, en la actualidad ya son superiores al 4% que, aunque podría parecer ahora todavía reducida en términos reales, su servicio se ha cuadruplicado en estos meses, es decir se ha multiplicado por cuatro.
Esta situación se complica aún más por la reducción o suspensión del apoyo de los Estados Unidos a la OTAN, en un momento en que se incrementa la percepción de que el gobierno ruso podría invadir otros países en aquel continente. Por lo mismo se ha acordado que los países miembros de esta organización dediquen el 5% de su PIB a incrementar el gasto militar, lo que elevaría su déficit fiscal aún más.
Como resultado, el gasto público se tiene que reducir en otras áreas de la sociedad, resultando en los conflictos mencionados. Esto tiene un fuerte impacto en todos los países y se agrava por el bajo crecimiento económico de los últimos años, debido a los elevados impuestos y las regulaciones que las distintas empresas tienen en aquella zona del mundo. Durante varios años los distintos gobiernos se han caracterizado por dar un mayor énfasis a la distribución del ingreso, a los apoyos sociales y a mejoras a la población.
Como resultado de lo anterior, las empresas han perdido competitividad frente a otros países, lo que resulta en un bajo crecimiento económico. Resalta la reducción de los programas energéticos que permitirían una reducción de los costos de las empresas, resaltando la cancelación de los programas nucleares para generar energía eléctrica. Por otro lado, la apertura de sus economías a la competencia de países de menores costos como China y Vietnam, generó que las empresas de la zona hayan tenido una reducción en sus ventas resaltando la industria automotriz y otras más.

title: What does Celtic's demolition of Hearts mean for Hogh?
summary: What does Celtic's demolition of Hearts mean for Hogh? - Published Celtic's mauling of Hearts eliminated many of the question marks hanging over Martin O'Neill's side - but one significant question remains. What does Sunday's incredible seven-goal victory tell us about record signing Kasper Hogh's p...
content:
What does Celtic's demolition of Hearts mean for Hogh?
- Published
Celtic's mauling of Hearts eliminated many of the question marks hanging over Martin O'Neill's side - but one significant question remains.
What does Sunday's incredible seven-goal victory tell us about record signing Kasper Hogh's place in the team?
Benched for the visit of last season's Scottish Premiership runners-up, a dynamic front three of Camilo Duran, Callum Osmand and Haissem Hassan were integral to a scintillating attacking display.
In the aftermath of last Thursday's chastening Europa League defeat at Benfica, during which Hogh was hooked at half-time, O'Neill backed the 25-year-old to end the campaign with 20 goals.
But is the £11m man now fighting for a starting spot?
Hogh struggling to find feet at Celtic
Having scored in just one of his 12 Celtic appearances - a hat-trick at Kilmarnock in August - O'Neill acknowledges his marquee summer acquisition is low on confidence, with a Europa League match against Celta Vigo to come on Thursday.
"He has lost a bit of confidence, but we will get that back during the course of time," the veteran boss said in the lead-up to Sunday's demolition of Hearts.
"We have game after game after game between now and January, but he will score goals for us, there is no question about it, and it is just a matter of tinkering around, but that's the nature of the business."
The Denmark forward did come off the bench at the weekend to set up Benjamin Nygren for Celtic's seventh goal. He also assisted the Sweden midfielder during the 2-0 win at Motherwell seven days earlier.
However, Hogh's performance in the 4-1 defeat in Lisbon, sandwiched between those two Premiership victories, intensified the debate surrounding his place in the team.
"If I'm a creative player and I've got Duran and Hogh to pick from, I'm taking Duran every day of the week," former Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said.
"He looks to get off the side of defenders. If you put a ball into the area, he's more likely to be alive to it."
Hogh was brought off at the break in Lisbon, with Duran, who has been the standout of Celtic's summer arrivals, moved to the centre of the attack.
With Hassan and Osmand on either side, O'Neill's frontline looked far more potent in a much-improved second-half display.
The same trio that finished Thursday's match started on Sunday, and Hearts simply could not live with them.
An Osmand double helped the champions establish a 5-1 half-time lead, while Duran's ninth goal of the campaign was one of two Celtic goals after the break.
Europa League: Celtic v Celta Vigo
Thursday, 22 October (20:00 BST)
Celtic Park, Glasgow
Listen to live match commentary on BBC Sounds and follow text updates on the BBC Sport website and app.
'Celtic's best attack doesn't include Hogh'
It seems inconceivable that an £11m signing would not be a guaranteed starter for a Scottish club.
That said, Celtic fans were encouraged to see Hogh embrace fellow forward Osmand as he left the pitch at half-time on Sunday.
There is therefore nothing to suggest, from the outside, that ego will get in the way if the Dane spends time out of the first-choice XI.
Sunday's emphatic 7-1 victory has gone some way towards settling the debate, at least for now: Celtic's best forward line appears to be one that does not include their record signing.
"There have been question marks over whether Celtic's best attack involves Hogh. For me, it doesn't," BBC Scotland pundit Andy Halliday said on The Monday Night Club.
The former Hearts, Rangers and Motherwell midfielder added: "There's no doubt there's a goalscorer in there with Hogh. You don't score in the Champions League against Manchester City, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid if you're not. He's just a goalscorer who isn't scoring goals."
The same cannot be said of Duran, who is thriving in a Celtic shirt and has 14 goal contributions - nine goals and five assists - in 15 games, many of which have come while playing in a wide role.
However, O'Neill has said that the Colombia international prefers to play centrally, and Halliday believes he can offer Celtic much more in that position - but what does that mean for Hogh?
"You look at Duran as a number nine on Sunday, the part he plays in the third goal, the fourth goal," Halliday said.
"When Jamie McCart takes a loose touch, Hogh wouldn't be close enough or quick enough to get on to that loose ball and spring Celtic into attack. Duran isn't just a goalscorer, he's so much more than that - and you saw that on Sunday.
"O'Neill still reckons Hogh will score 20 goals this season. It's hard to suggest he wouldn't, given his previous record at Bodo/Glimt, but at this moment in time, he isn't doing enough to be in Celtic's attack.
"O'Neill's searching for his best team and best front three, and the three you saw on Sunday are that."

title: Joseph Pilates, creador del método de entrenamiento: “La correcta postura sólo será posible cuando el mecanismo completo de funcionamiento del cuerpo esté bajo control”
summary: Un móvil de LN+ dialogó con la instructora Melani Giommetti, quien sostuvo que “la actividad sirve para fortalecer nuestros músculos de forma consciente y a largo plazo” - 3 minutos de lectura' Un móvil de LN+ fue hasta el centro de entrenamiento Toulouse, ubicado en el barrio porteño de Palermo, pa...
content:
Un móvil de LN+ dialogó con la instructora Melani Giommetti, quien sostuvo que “la actividad sirve para fortalecer nuestros músculos de forma consciente y a largo plazo”
- 3 minutos de lectura'
Un móvil de LN+ fue hasta el centro de entrenamiento Toulouse, ubicado en el barrio porteño de Palermo, para dialogar con la instructora de pilates Melani Giommetti, quien reveló qué son las cadenas miofasciales: la serie de ejercicios que revolucionaron esta práctica deportiva que no para de sumar adeptos.
Joseph Pilates, el creador del método de entrenamiento, solía recordar: “Somos arquitectos de nuestra vida”. En la misma línea, enfatizaba: “La felicidad está subordinada al bienestar físico por encima del nivel social o económico”.
“Acá en nuestro instituto tenemos nuestra propia investigación y promovemos la práctica del pilates a través de las cadenas miofasciales”, manifestó Giommetti. “Esto consiste en ver el cuerpo de forma integral, y no como grupos musculares aislados”.
Sobre la práctica de la disciplina, la instructora explicó: “La cama, que se llama reformer, es una herramienta clave. Porque no solo nos asiste, sino que también nos potencia para que no sea solo un trabajo pasivo”.
Dos mitos
Como suele darse en diversas disciplinas deportivas, la instructora despejó dos mitos relativos a la práctica de pilates.
“No es verdadero eso de que, al trabajar en una cama, no se trabaje tanto. En el pilates se trabaja mucho utilizando pesas y nuestro propio peso”, sostuvo Giommetti y agregó: “Otro mito es que sea una práctica solo para mujeres”.
En palabras de la especialista, “cada vez más hombres vienen y practican, porque pilates potencia muchas de otras disciplinas particulares que ellos mismos realizan”.
Cómodo y barato
Consultada sobre la vestimenta y el costo de hacer pilates, Giommetti detalló que “lo mejor es siempre practicar con ropa cómoda, preferentemente pantalón corto y descalzos”.
Sobre los valores, apuntó: “Practicar pilates no es costoso: las cuatro clases hoy rondan los $80.000, y vale la pena”.
Quién fue Joseph Pilates
Joseph Pilates fue un entrenador físico nacido en Alemania a fines del siglo XIX que desarrolló un método de ejercicios enfocado en fortalecer el cuerpo a través del control de los movimientos, la respiración y la alineación postural. Desde joven se interesó por distintas disciplinas como la gimnasia, el boxeo y el yoga, conocimientos que más tarde combinaría en un sistema propio.
Durante la Primera Guerra Mundial comenzó a perfeccionar su técnica mientras trabajaba con personas lesionadas, utilizando incluso resortes y mecanismos adaptados a camas hospitalarias para ayudar en la rehabilitación física. Aquellas experiencias serían la base de varios de los aparatos que hoy se utilizan en las clases de pilates.
En la década de 1920 se instaló en Nueva York junto a su esposa, Clara, donde abrió un estudio que rápidamente ganó popularidad entre bailarines, atletas y artistas. Su método, al que llamó inicialmente “Contrología”, buscaba integrar mente y cuerpo mediante movimientos precisos y conscientes.
Tras su muerte en 1967, sus discípulos continuaron difundiendo sus enseñanzas. Con el tiempo, el sistema pasó a conocerse simplemente como pilates y se convirtió en una de las prácticas de acondicionamiento físico más populares del mundo.
